Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
 
 
**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

**Plant Manager**

**Treatment, Storage, and Disposal Facility**

Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking a Plant Manager

for our Casa Grande, AZ plant.

 

 

We are looking for an experienced Plant Manager to lead our hazardous waste operations, non-hazardous waste consolidation, and recycling services in Casa Grande, Arizona. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in both hazardous and non-hazardous waste management. This role requires a hands-on professional who can collaborate closely with our Vice President of Disposal Services to enhance safety, ensure compliance, and maximize hazardous waste throughput.

Triumvirate Environmental provides leading organizations in the higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing sectors with diverse services and expertise to assist them with compli
ance management. At Triumvirate Environmental, we strive to WOW both our employees and our customers. Our unique culture fosters growth, development, education, and creativity.  

 

**Responsibilities:**

 

* Oversee the Hazardous Waste, Non-Hazardous Waste, and Recycling Operations in Casa Grande, AZ.
* Ensure that all permitted activities are in full compliance.
* Ensure safety of our staff working at the plant.
* Hire and retain employees.
* Oversee construction for second phase of the facility.
* Oversee all related logistics activities.
* Establish Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s) to drive competitive costs and recycling value to our clients.
* Analyze and assess industry and market dynamics on a regular basis.
* Maintain and cultivate relationships with customers and vendors; establish customer retention and growth strategies; develop multi-level/multi-discipline business relations at customer  and vendor accounts.
* Build relationships with local and state agencies (fire dept., health dept., licensing bureaus, Department of Environmental Quality, etc.)
* Advise the company on market opportunities beyond Arizona.
* Advise the company on capital expenditures necessary to advance the company’s overall objectives for the facility.
* Develop technical expertise and knowledge of the company’s services and product lines.
* Achieve annual sales and gross margin targets.
* Participate in the annual budget process and prepare product forecasts as necessary.
* Manage resolution of customer related issues.
* Provide market information and intelligence.
* Share recommendations with the executive team for new products, services and identified areas of optimization.

**Ba
sic Requirements:**

 

* Bachelors degree is required
* 10-15 years’ experience within the hazardous and non-hazardous waste business.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to build, lead team, provide direction to staff and senior management.
* Specific experience importing/exporting hazardous waste between the nations of Mexico and the United States.
* Strong technical knowledge along with financial knowledge.
* Possess negotiating, strategic, and tactical transportation, planning, warehousing and logistics, problem analysis, and creativity skills.
* Experience running national and/or international field services operations.
* Expertise in all MS suite applications with strong Excel skills.
* Strong financial acumen with excellent numerical skills.
* Experience with various hazardous waste treatment processes including but not limited to fuel blending, neutralization, stabilization, evaporation and repackaging of various waste streams.
* Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship
* Must have
 a reliable form of transportation
* Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC)
* Upon employment, you will be required to participate in a random drug screening program (inclusive of THC) as part of our company’s commitment to maintaining a safe and healthy work environment
* Must be able to lift 60 pounds on a regular basis

**Preferred Requirements:**

 

* Master’s degree
* Bilingual English & Spanish

 

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!  

 

To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on


LinkedIn,

Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our


website

! 

 

Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.

 

If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at


https://www.triumvirate.com/contact

or call us at 888-834-9697.  The requirements listed above are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. To view our California Privacy Notice and Policy, click


here

new_roles.description:
Job ID: 530934
 
 
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
 
 
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
 
 
**Job Summary**
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
 
 
**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Midlothian, TX.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.

new_roles.description:
**Job Description**
The Plant Manager will oversee operations which include environmental, health & safety, quality, production, maintenance, capital planning and execution in a cost-effective manner while meeting all customer requirements.
 
 
**Essential Duties/Responsibilities**
Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.
 
 

* Support, mentor and develop plant management and supervisory personnel through regular coaching and formal development tools.
* Lead all safety improvement initiatives and create a safety-based culture.
* Ensure ongoing compliance with all regulatory agencies including, OSHA, EPA, HACCP and other local and regional agencies.
* Prepare monthly reports, analyze financial budgets and take corrective measures as needed.
* Maintain efficient and timely flow of all raw materials received and ingredients shipped.
* Lead continuous improvement efforts in all areas of responsibility.
* Review and lead local Capital Projects, planning process to ensure compliance and development of assets for ongoing success and improvement.
* Ensure all personnel properly trained and equipment is in good working order to meet ongoing and future business needs.
* Assure all finish product shipped is in accordance with all quality standards and specifications.
* Effectively manage and reduce energy use at facility.
* Manage local purchasing activities.
* All other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* High School diploma or GED equivalent.
* Minimum 3+ years of experience in a supervisory/ management position in an industrial or plant setting.
* Rendering industry experience is a definite plus.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree preferred; Engineering degree is an asset.
* Labor relations background and leadership preferred.
* Detail oriented; highly organized.
* Ability to work well with internal staff.
* Exceptional written and oral communication skills.
* Self-starter; self-motivated.
* Good math and computer skills.

**Working Environment**
Occasionally = up to 20% Frequently = up to 21% to 50% Constantly - at least 51%
 
 

* Exposed to unpleasant or disagreeable physical environments such as high noise level, strong odors, and/or exposure to heat and cold: Constantly
* Exposed to bio hazardous conditions: Constantly
* Exposed to toxic or caustic chemicals which mandate attention to safety considerations: Constantly
* Exposed to Electrical hazards; risk of electrical shock: Frequently
* Handles or works with potentially dangerous equipment: Constantly

**Physical Demands**
Occasionally = up to 20% Frequently = up to 21% to 50% Constantly - at least 51%
 
 

* Must be able to remain in a stationary position: Frequently
* Must be able to move about inside/outside office or work location: Frequently
* Operates a computer and other office machinery: Frequently
* Must be able to position oneself to maintain computers in the lab, including under desks and in the server closet: Frequently
* Must be able to ascend/descend on a ladder: Frequently
* Must be able to use senses to; effectively communicate with co-workers and clients and detect hazardous conditions: Frequently
* Must be able to occasionally lift up to 50lbs

**About Us**
We’re one of the world’s leading practitioners of circularity, transforming materials from the animal agriculture and food industries into valuable ingredients. Ingredients that nourish people, feed animals and crops, and fuel the world with renewable energy.
 
 
**About The Team**
Darling Ingredients is an equal opportunity employer and gives consideration to qualified applicants without regard to race, color, creed, religion, age, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military service, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state and local law. * Paid weekly

* Ability to work in all weather conditions.
* Ability to stand for extended periods of time at conveyor belt operation.
* Ability to climb heights of 20 feet on a regular basis.
* Ability to lift, carry, and/or pull 50 pounds on a regular basis.
* Ability to work in dusty, wet, and loud environment.
* Required to wear safety equipment including hard hat, safety glasses, goggles, steel toed boots, ear plugs, gloves and various other similar items as required or needed.

**A bit about us:**
Headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri with more than 1,200 employees and nearing $2B in revenue. A diversified construction company that partners with leading organizations throughout North America to build their most challenging and important projects.
 
 
Provides construction solutions to the automotive, commercial, civil, energy, food & beverage, healthcare, heavy industrial, industrial process, and water industries.
 
 
Our Values:
 
 
Working Safely
 
Valuing Diversity
 
Serving Humbly
 
Executing with Integrity
 
Solving Creatively
 
Engaging Fully
 
 
 
**Why join us?**
Profit-sharing plan, cash bonus programs and annual cost-of-living adjustments
 
Generous salary increases and per diems for qualified out-of-town assignments
 
Health, dental and vision insurance eligibility on day one
 
Paid parental leave
 
Continuing education reimbursement
 
Personalized career development and training programs
 
Minimum of 29 days of PTO (including holidays) for entry-level roles
 
Fitness center for St. Louis office-based team members
 
Gym membership reimbursement for project-based team members
 
Corporate office cafeteria access
 
Employee Resource Group (ERG) opportunities
 
Philanthropy opportunities
 
 
 
**Job Details**
The Plant Manager directs and manages all plant operations with overall responsibilities for production, maintenance, quality and other production-related activities as a part of a premier structural steel fabricator and erector.
 
 
Essential Responsibilities & Duties include the following; however, other duties may be assigned. The Company provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with a disability, unless doing so poses an undue hardship on the Company. To be a qualified individual, an employee must be able to perform each of the essential functions of his or her job with or without a reasonable accommodation.
 
 
Directs and manages Responsible for labor relations and managing union issues associated with craft labor.
 
Manages capital asset maintenance.
 
Establishes and monitors overall plant performance for production and quality standards.
 
Controls and minimizes repair expenses.
 
Maintains existing plant facilities and equipment; replaces or makes adjustments to plant facilities and equipment when necessary.
 
Provides leadership and training to accomplish Company goals and objectives.
 
Implements and maintains preventative maintenance programs.
 
Incorporates shop floor organization and plant cleanliness among plant personnel.
 
Manages and directs non-supervisory administrative or union employees and is responsible for the overall direction and management of these employees.
 
Travels to Company and subsidiary offices; offsite client, subcontractor, and supplier meetings; and other locations across North America to fulfill the essential duties of the role as required.
 
Exhibits regular and reliable attendance in person as required by the Supervisor, Company guidelines, and/or project and office obligations.
 
Education and Experience
 
 
Bachelor's degree and 5 years’ plant/general management experience in a manufacturing environment, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
 
 
Experience managing in a union environment required.
 
Working knowledge of budgets and financials statements required.
 
Background with manufacturing methods, process improvement programs and procedures required.

By applying for this job, you agree to receive calls, AI-generated calls, text messages, or emails from Jobot, and/or its agents and contracted partners. Frequency varies for text messages. new_roles.description:
**Plant Manager**
**Why Byrne**
At Byrne, we foster a culture built on teamwork, excellence, and professionalism. Our greatest strength lies in the exceptional talent and dedication of our team members across every part of the organization. We value their contributions and ensure they’re recognized, rewarded, and compensated in ways that reflect their impact and expertise.
 
 
**Pay And Benefits**

* Salary Range – $125,000 - $152,500 per year
* Competitive bonus programs
* Medical, Dental, Vision benefits available day 1 of employment
* Supplemental benefits available on day 30 of employment
* Eligible for 401 (k) with a company match available on day 90 of employment
* Educational Support via tuition reimbursement and scholarship program

**Work Shift and Location**
3156 Byrne Hollow Crossing Cortland, NY 13045
 
 
Monday – Friday normal business hours. This may require evening, night and weekend availability based on business needs.
 
 
**Job Overview**
The Plant Manager plays a key role in executing assigned Production tasks. This includes leading various teams in production efforts in addition to performing the duties as needed to efficiently facilitate plant operations. The Plant Manager is also responsible for ensuring that the plant products manufactured conform to company-defined product quality standards, as well as Federal, State, and local standards of product identity, safety, and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs).
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of the plant; coordinate and direct plant operations in the achievement of production, cost, quality, and safety objectives.
* Ensure an appropriate volume of production and raw inventories for each product produced to maximize machine efficiencies and minimize down time and stock outs.
* Manage plant budget and expenses to fall within, or better than plan. Manage all plant variances to meet or exceed plan including, but not limited to, headcount, overtime, and spending.
* Ensure that the quality of products produced at the facility is consistent with intended design and desired image.
* Coordinate with Plant Production Scheduler, Warehouse Management and Supply Management to ensure needed dry goods are on-hand as required.
* Establish and administer mechanisms for being alerted when suppliers are going to be late for delivery or cut items on a delivery. Take action to minimize impact on production schedules and alert appropriate sales and logistics personnel.
* Provide planning assistance with physical inventories and provide staffing to perform these activities; ensure accuracy of all inventories at all times.
* Ensure reporting mechanism regarding KPI are in-place and functioning; ensure monthly reporting of critical KPI to company leadership and plant staff.
* Monitor intake procedures of raw dairy products to assure quality standards are met and production shortages are avoided.
* Contributes to the development of budgets and cost controls. Ensure direct reports analyze, budget, and control spending for their respective line accounts.
* Facilitate the development of strategies and corrective actions to resolve quality issues as necessary.
* Implements and maintains manufacturing policies, procedures, and production control programs.
* Must ensure full compliance with all quality assurance standards.
* Provide for the development, prioritization, and execution of capital improvement projects within the facility.
* Provide leadership for effective employee relations through positive communication, coaching, training, problem resolution/corrective actions, and floor time, work cooperatively with Human Resources.
* Coordinate production activities with purchasing, sales, warehousing, distribution, maintenance, and quality control activities to obtain optimum production and utilization of staff and equipment.
* Provide for the personal and professional growth of team through coaching, feedback, and opportunity.
* Foster participation of the workforce to enhance awareness and cooperation.
* Ensure compliance with company policies and all government regulations; Ensure compliance and enforcement of all work rules and regulations to plant operations and all applicable employees.
* Ensure proper GMP and sanitation procedures are followed plant-wide in collaboration with the quality unit.
* Communicate with Human Resource Department on needs of the facility.
* Rigorously assess your leadership and technical team in terms of values, adherence to SOPs/GMPs, and actual results.
* Foster an “open door” policy for all employees to maintain an open line of communication between direct reports and management staff.
* Promote and provide excellent customer service for all customers.
* Promote a safe and harmonious work environment and adherence to company policy and procedures.
* Responsible for ensuring direct reports assigned duties and responsibilities are covered during planned and unplanned absence from work, including acting as a backup as necessary.

**Min. Qualifications**

* BA/BS in Business Administration or related field, with an MBA preferred.
* Minimum 5-7 years in the role of Managing a Production facility.
* Related experience in the dairy food industry.
* Certifications to include but not limited to CPT, HACCP, OSHA 10-hour, First Aid, CPR and AED.

**Byrne**
Headquartered in LaFayette, Byrne is a Central New York-based dairy company with a legacy spanning over 90 years. Its operations include an extended shelf-life (ESL) and ultra-high temperature (UHT) pasteurization plant in DeWitt, as well as an ESL manufacturing facility in Cortlandville. Byrne also maintains warehouse facilities in Syracuse and East Syracuse, along with a dedicated ice cream center in Syracuse. As a recognized industry leader, Byrne continues to drive innovation at the forefront of dairy processing and product development.

new_roles.description:
At WK Kellogg Co, we exist to create joy and connection to inspire Gr-r-reat days. We believe that doing good is always good for business and we have stood for this since Kellogg Company was founded more than 120 years ago. We are passionate about doing our part to make nutritious foods, create social connectivity and respect natural resources. Together, these actions create positive progress for people and the planet – today and for years to come. We have big plans for how we are going to accomplish this, and we would love for you to join us in this effort.
 
 
**The most compelling leadership opportunities aren’t always about stepping into something already built. Sometimes they’re about helping shape what comes next.**
The
**Senior Manager, Plant Operations**
leads the strategic and operational direction of multiple business units within a high-performing, large-scale, 24/7 manufacturing operation, and line-centric manufacturing platform.
 
 
This role drives excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development by empowering Operations Managers, Supervisors, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
 
 
**You won’t simply inherit an operation. You’ll have the opportunity to help build what comes next.**
**Working Relationships Include**

* Reports to: Plant Director
* Supervises: Operations Managers and Supervisors
* Peer Relationships: KSUM, Quality Manager, Sr. RM Manager, HR Manager, EHS Manager, E& F Manager, KIWS Coach
* Key Contacts: Internal – Plant Leadership Team, Corporate Operations, Engineering, KIWS, HR; External – Vendors, Contractors, and Corporate Support Functions

**Here’s What You Will Be Doing**

* Strategic Leadership: Set direction and priorities for assigned business units, ensuring alignment with plant goals and corporate strategy.
* Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop Operations Managers and Supervisor to build high-performing teams and future leaders.
* Operational Oversight: Ensure consistent execution of production plans and consistently deliver strong results across key plant KPIs, including safety, quality, food safety, cost, and service.
* Innovation & Project Execution: Lead the excellent execution of innovation and projects entering the plant, ensuring effective planning, cross-functional alignment, and successful implementation.
* Budgeting & Planning: Own the business planning and budgeting process for assigned units, including cost containment and resource allocation.
* Lean & CI Deployment: Champion and sustain lean manufacturing principles and WK Kellogg Integrated Work Systems (KIWS) across all units.
* Culture & Engagement: Drive a culture of safety, accountability, and engagement, promoting continuous learning and recognition.
* Compliance & Standards: Ensure compliance with all regulatory and internal standards related to safety, food safety, sanitation, and labor relations.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with support functions and external stakeholders to optimize performance and resolve complex challenges.

**Work Environment**

* This role is based within a 24/7 union manufacturing facility.
* Must be flexible to work any shift and travel up to 25%
* Regular presence on the production floor required
* Frequent interaction with internal teams and external partners

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing
* Proven success in leading large teams and managing multiple production lines
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement systems
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others and build effective teams
* Excellent strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
* Experience in union environments preferred
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and SAP
* Experience with budget creation and performance management
* Experience working within a 24/7 manufacturing environment is preferred

***Salary Range:***

*$164,160 - $205,200*
*Salary pay ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, certifications, qualifications, relevant education or training, and local market conditions.*
*At WK Kellogg Co, our success depends on our most vital asset — our people. That’s why we’re committed to providing you with benefits and programs that support your Total Health and your journey to be and feel your best — physically, financially, emotionally, and socially.*
*Although subject to change, the below are the benefits currently offered in association with this position:*

* Incentive Plan bonus eligibility
* Health, dental and vision insurance
* Savings and Investment Plan with Company match and contribution
* Paid Time Off (includes paid sick time)
* 11 Paid Holidays
* Life Insurance, AD and D Insurance and STD/LTD
* Tuition reimbursement, adoption assistance for eligible employees
* Employee recognition program

*The above offerings are subject to the terms of WKKC policies, which will control in the event of a conflict with the above descriptions*
*Our comprehensive and competitive benefits not only deliver value to you and your family, but also offer choice to meet your unique needs and knowledge to empower confident decision-making.*
**About Wk Kellogg Co**
*At WK Kellogg Co, we bring our best to everyone, every day through our trusted foods and brands. Our journey began in 1894, when our founder W.K. Kellogg reimagined the future of food with the creation of Corn Flakes, changing breakfast forever. Since then, we have embraced the same spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship in everything we do, channeling our founder’s passion and commitment to creating high quality and delicious products while fostering communities. Our iconic brand portfolio includes Frosted Flakes, Rice Krispies, Froot Loops, Kashi, Special K, Raisin Bran, Frosted Mini Wheats, and Bear Naked. With a presence in the majority of households across North America, our brands play a key role in enhancing the lives of millions of consumers every day, promoting a strong sense of physical, emotional and societal wellbeing. Our beloved brand characters, including Tony the Tiger and Toucan Sam, represent our deep connections with the consumers and communities we serve. For more information, visit*
*www.wkkellogg.com*
*.*

*If we can help you with a reasonable accommodation throughout the application or hiring process, please email TalentAssist@wkkellogg.com*
***THE FINER PRINT***
*The ability to work a full shift, come to work on time, work overtime as needed and the ability to work according to the necessary schedule to meet job requirements with or without reasonable accommodation is an essential function of this position.*

*link*

new_roles.title: Senior Manager of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Senior Manager of Operations - Austin, TX**

**DESCRIPTION:**

We’re seeking a hands-on Sr. Operations Manager with experience scaling silicon-based products in a semiconductor company. This player-coach role owns the operational path from foundry and wafer production through test, backend processing, and manufacturing. You’ll qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, establish and strengthen quality-control measures, and drive consistent quality, yield, cost, and delivery as production grows.

Experience with RFID inlay production is especially relevant.

**What you’ll do:**

* Own foundry relationships from negotiation through production execution, and scale wafer level production.
* Manage wafer-test facility relationships; evaluate and qualify test partners, and select test equipment to optimize cost, quality, and throughput.
* Lead test development, wafer backend operations, yield improvement, reliability, and failure analysis.
* Qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, including overseeing end-to-end inlay production and its ramp to volume.
* Establish and improve quality-control measures, operating procedures, and RMA processes.
* Monitor supplier quality, conduct supply-chain audits, and resolve manufacturing, quality, and delivery issues.
* Establish and improve ERP/MRP processes, WIP tracking, inventory planning, and production controls.
* Develop cost models, negotiate contracts, and drive improvements in cost, quality, and delivery.
* Manage one direct report and coordinate work across four internal engineers and executive stakeholders, including the CEO.

**What you’ll bring:**

* BSEE or equivalent practical experience.
* 7–10 years of operations, manufacturing, or related experience in a semiconductor company.
* Experience with RFID inlay manufacturing is a plus.
* Hands-on experience with silicon-based products and semiconductor manufacturing operations.
* Experience scaling products from wafer fabrication and test through backend processing and volume production.
* Experience working with foundries, wafer-test facilities, and manufacturing vendors.
* Familiarity with yield optimization, reliability, quality assurance, supplier audits, failure analysis, ERP/MRP systems, WIP tracking, and inventory planning.
* Strong communication, coordination, and negotiation skills, with a practical, roll-up-your sleeves approach.

new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary**
The Senior Manager, Global Innovation, oversees performance management, operational excellence, and strategic execution for manufacturing entities across Asia, including Vietnam, China, and South Korea. Serves as a key liaison between headquarters and regional production sites, driving data‑driven decision‑making, productivity improvements, and process standardization.
 
 
**Job Description**
**Key Responsibilities**

* Performance Management & Financial Oversight
* Monitor and evaluate the operational and financial performance of manufacturing subsidiaries in Asia
* Develop and manage KPIs
* Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with regional leadership
* Identify performance gaps and implement corrective action plans
* Strategic Planning & Execution
* Formulate mid- to long-term manufacturing and supply chain strategies aligned with global business objectives
* Support capacity planning, cost optimization, and footprint strategy (e.g., China+1, nearshoring)
* Conduct market and operational feasibility analysis for new investments or expansions
* Operational Excellence & Process Improvement
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives across production sites (Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen)
* Standardize processes and implement best practices across regions
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Procurement, Logistics, Quality, R&D) to improve end-to-end efficiency
* HQ–Regional Coordination
* Act as the primary liaison between HQ and Asia manufacturing teams
* Ensure alignment on corporate policies, reporting standards, and operational priorities
* Facilitate communication, issue resolution, and project execution across time zones
* Data Analytics & Reporting
* Build and maintain dashboards and reporting systems for real-time performance tracking
* Analyze large datasets to generate actionable insights and executive-level reports
* Support digital transformation initiatives (ERP, MES, data integration)

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or related field (MBA preferred)
* 7–10+ years of experience in manufacturing, supply chain, or operations strategy roles
* Proven experience managing or overseeing operations in Asia (Vietnam, China, Korea preferred)
* Strong analytical skills with proficiency in Excel, Power BI/Tableau, or similar tools
* Deep understanding of manufacturing KPIs and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma)
* Experience working in a global, matrixed organization

**Preferred Skills**

* Familiarity with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, etc.)
* Multilingual capability (Korean, Chinese, or Vietnamese is a plus)
* Strong project management and stakeholder management skills
* Ability to travel internationally (20–40%)

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality SME (HV/Substation)
new_roles.description:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Department: EHSQ / Quality
 
 
Location: Houston, TX
 
 
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
 
 
Direct Reports: None
 
 
FLSA Status: Exempt
 
 
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
 
 
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
 
 
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation)
 
 
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
 
 
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
 
 
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (HV & Substation) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on high-voltage, substation, and transmission construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on HV and substation scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers collector substations, switchyards and points of interconnection, and generation tie-lines (gen-tie); medium-voltage collection systems remain within the scope of Electrical Quality.
 
 
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active HV, substation, or gen-tie construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of HV and substation Quality across the portfolio.
 
 
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors, combined with the judgment to translate engineering, utility, manufacturer, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and Transmission & Distribution (T&D) teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, relay and protection settings, and functional commissioning remain with Engineering and Commissioning; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
 
 
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
 
 
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time."
 
 
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on HV, substation, switchyard, point of interconnection, and gen-tie construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for HV and substation scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, utility requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain HV and substation inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing HV, substation, or gen-tie scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying HV and substation-specific contract, utility, testing, and special inspection requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the HV & Substation Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, documentation requirements, and common HV and substation failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the HV and substation Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for HV, substation, and gen-tie scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring HV and substation nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, or subcontractor personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of major HV equipment, including power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, and control enclosures, in alignment with manufacturer requirements.
* Review acceptance test records and third-party test reports for completeness and conformance with ANSI/NETA ATS, project specifications, and manufacturer requirements, and coordinate Quality witness points with testing agencies and Commissioning.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in energization-readiness and turnover verification for HV and substation systems, while maintaining clear separation from relay settings, protection coordination, and functional commissioning responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of major HV equipment, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, and third-party agencies on HV and substation Quality matters, including utility inspection and witness requirements for facilities built to utility standards.
* Align closely with the Engineering and T&D teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects.
* Monitor HV and substation Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the HV and substation Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, T&D, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, utility, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, regions, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, electrical testing, protection and control, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, utilities, owners, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, substation, transmission, or industrial electrical construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on high-voltage substation or transmission projects; utility-scale PV electrical experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for HV and substation construction.
* Strong working knowledge of substation and HV construction, including grounding systems, foundations, structural steel, control enclosures, power transformers, circuit breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers, bus systems, station service equipment, cable and raceway systems, and transmission line structures and conductors.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, one-line and three-line diagrams, grounding plans, physical arrangement drawings, schematics and wiring diagrams, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer instructions.
* Experience reviewing electrical acceptance test documentation and third-party test reports against ANSI/NETA ATS and project specifications.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted HV and substation work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with interconnecting utilities, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and equipment manufacturers.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, protection and control, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ American Welding Society (AWS): Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
+ American Concrete Institute (ACI): Concrete Field Testing Technician, Grade I
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of power transformers, circuit breakers, switchgear, or control enclosures.
* Experience across multiple substation configurations, voltage classes, and equipment manufacturers, including facilities built to interconnecting utility standards and transferred to utility ownership.
* Experience with gen-tie transmission line construction, including foundations, steel structures, conductor and OPGW installation, and associated hardware.
* Working knowledge of NESC (IEEE C2), NEC (NFPA 70), ANSI/NETA ATS, IEEE 80, and IEEE C57 series standards for power transformers.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV and BESS projects with integrated substation and interconnection scopes.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
 
 

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, utilities, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access substation and HV construction areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access substation and HV construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, qualification requirements, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
 
 

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale substation, high-voltage, gen-tie, solar, and BESS construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized facilities as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, qualification boundaries, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, testing schedules, utility requirements, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.

new_roles.description:
At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it reality.
 
 
For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.
 
 
At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.
 
 
We are looking for a S
**r. Manager, Quality**
to join our team in one of today’s most exciting technologies. This role will report to
**Director of Quality**
and based in
**Newark, Delaware. This is a fully on-site, in office role 5 days a week**
.
 
 
**Role and Responsibilities:**

* Ensure 100% Quality assurance at the Skid line manufacturing through inspection, testing, and sub-component testing/inspection. Assist in hiring personnel needed to support this effort.
* Partner with Install Quality team (field) to understand real time (daily) what items are escaping the plant and instituting immediate mitigation plans including addressing any inventory in the pipeline not yet installed.
* Implement permanent corrective actions working with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply chain, or SQE as per relevance on each issue.
* Provide quality input into the new equipment being purchased for the scaling of Delaware manufacturing. Include inputs for quality assurance into equipment design, and verification of process steps. Understand and provide input into the planned operation, what can be bypassed, maintenance plans, calibration or drift of the equipment, automation that can fail and be undetected leading to quality escapes.
* Participate and understand results from testing in the plant; Functional test, Tommy test, FIT, etc. Drive pareto of failures to help cross functional problem solving of test failures.
* Implement a 100% functional test (new) on skid final product assembly; electrical continuity, communications integrity, piping assurance, start up simulation, etc. to assure 100% QA prior to shipping to customer.
* Ensure skid components and systems have latest FW revision prior to shipping to the W/H, or out of W/H to field.
* Work with CIG and Manufacturing Engr, and NPI to implement workload being removed from the customer install side and being moved into skid assembly. Provide oversight to ensure best quality achievement; ensure work instructions are clear, operators trained, workstations have proper tools, and judgement criteria.
* Collaborate with Supplier Quality / Suppliers to achieve zero-defect flow (“dock-to-stock”) for all purchased, contract manufacture parts, materials, and Bloom Energy manufactured parts.
* Drive component and design failures back to the earliest point of detection in the process.
* Ensure manufacturing process have Control plans with CTQ, and POA built in to each station.
* Work collaboratively with Design teams to DFM, through a “registration system”, and Pokeyoke assembly methods for highest quality assurance.
* Drive test excellence in the manufacturing plan to ensure that equipment and test stations are certified with robust qualification programs, that are documented and controlled for changes with proper accuracy and gage R&R techniques.
* Drive yield task forces to achieve company wide targets at each manufacturing point under this scope, with cross functional teams driving top pareto issues to RCCA.
* Ensure early engagement with the product engineering team to teach and perform early stage risk assessments (DFMEA et.al.)
* Design for manufacturability and reliability improvements during the early design stages of product development.
* Work with Engineering NPI and the manufacturing engineering teams to perform PFMEA, write work instructions, and establish quality check-points to guarantee zero-defect quality in production.
* Develop and implement formal, comprehensive process documentation including process flow diagrams, Process FMEAs, process control plans, operations method Sheets, manufacturing quality charts (MQCs) and etc.
* Lead critical problem solving task forces with emphasis on cross functional inputs, accountability, time to RCCA, and ensurance of mitigation of inventory, or field units at risk.
* Troubleshoot product issues by reviewing engineering drawings and design requirements. Drive a rigorous resolution process for product quality, reliability and design issues.
* Perform data-driven root cause failure analyses for design, manufacturing, and administrative problems.
* Perform process audits to monitor, continuously improve, and sustain superior product quality.
* Demonstrate the ability to interface and work collaboratively across departments internally and with suppliers and customers, (including Purchasing, Quality, R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Marketing and Finance), while building strong and cooperative working relationships.
* Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) Reduction: Establish and govern site COPQ metrics (scrap, rework, sorting, and warranty risk); lead cross-functional yield-improvement blitzes targeting measurable cost reductions and scrap minimization.
* Process Capability & Zero-Defect Mentality: Drive process capability (C\_p / C\_{pk} \ge 1.33) across critical-to-quality (CTQ) operations (welding, brazing, ceramic stack assembly, plumbing/gas-delivery, and electrical integration).

**Skills and Experience:**

* More than 10 years of increasing responsibility in the areas of Quality, and Manufacturing .
* Experience implementing company-wide ISO 9001 procedures and TS16949 standards and related process documentation. Possess working knowledge of process capability and control requirements, methods and systems.
* Demonstrated track record of building, restructuring, or significantly scaling a manufacturing quality team during rapid production ramp-up
* Proven successful application of multi-discipline engineering problem solving techniques.
* Understand the critical elements of modern Manufacturing Statistical Process Control, (e.g., practical working knowledge and experience with SPC, Process Capability, Cp, Cpk, etc.)
* Understand the critical elements of modern Reliability Engineering, (e.g., MCF, MTBF, MTT, etc.)
* Certification in a recognized problem-solving methodology such as six-sigma Black Belt, 8D, or Global Problem Solving.
* Strong verbal/active listening/written communications.
* Demonstrate planning and leadership skills.
* Expert with metrology, calibration, and Gage R & R’s.
* Ability to train in Quality System Auditing.
* Fluent in product phase-gate, NPI and technology transfer.
* Expertise in applying PPAP, First Article Inspections (FAI) and Reports).
* Strong critical thinking, analytical skills, and problem solving.
* Ability to effectively work within a very intense, dynamic, fast-paced, and demanding work environment.
* Familiarity with industry codes and quality standards applicable to clean power systems (ISO 9001:2015 required; working knowledge of ASME, NFPA, or UL standards preferred).
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality / Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE) and ASQ Certified Reliability Engineer (CRE) alongside CQE and Six Sigma Black Belt.
* Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office Suite and statistical software.
* Possess a passion for excellence.
* Unrestricted willingness to travel to all regions. Travel may be up to 25% of time.
* BS, MS or PhD in Mechanical/Material Science/Chemical/Electrical/Systems Engineering.
* Direct experience managing high-temperature fluidics/gas delivery, welding/brazing, ceramic integration, power electronics, or structural enclosures is a strong plus.

Bloom Energy is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We are committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. All qualified applicants, will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability. Bloom Energy makes reasonable accommodations, consistent with applicable laws, for the known physical or mental limitations of an otherwise qualified applicant or employee with a disability, who can perform the essential job functions, unless undue hardship would result.
 
 
At Bloom Energy, we are committed to supporting the well-being of our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees includes competitive Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with a large employer contribution, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with company match, generous Mental Health Support services, Legal services, virtual Physical Therapy access, and Fertility & Family Forming benefits.
 
 
Bloom Energy is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The total compensation for this position includes standard company benefits and is based on various factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience.
 
 
Salary Ranges:
 
 
$149,300.00 - $214,700.00

new_roles.title: Sr Manager, Quality Assurance Engineering (Hybrid - Acton, MA)
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary**
This Senior Manager, Quality Engineering role is a key leadership position responsible for overseeing Insulet’s global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team and ensuring new and modified Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred, validated, and sustained in compliance with FDA and ISO quality standards. The position leads a team of Quality Engineers supporting product launches, manufacturing expansion, process validation, risk management, CAPA, and continuous improvement initiatives across global manufacturing sites. The ideal candidate brings extensive medical device quality experience, deep expertise in design transfer, process validation, and regulatory compliance, along with proven people leadership skills. Success in this role requires partnering across Manufacturing, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, and Quality organizations to drive quality strategy, support global growth initiatives, and maintain high standards in a complex, high-volume regulated manufacturing environment.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality Engineering leads Insulet's global Design Transfer Quality Engineering team, ensuring new and changed Omnipod products and manufacturing processes are successfully transferred to production, validated and sustained in compliance with the Insulet Quality System, FDA Quality Management System Regulation (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485 and ISO 14971. The Sr. Quality Engineering Manager leads a team of Quality Engineers to support design transfer, capacity expansion, and process controls across Insulet's manufacturing sites. The Senior Manager establishes quality strategy, owns key QMS procedures and metrics, represents Quality throughout major design transfer and global expansion initiatives, and partners closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, R&D, Regulatory Affairs and site Quality leaders. The ideal candidate is an experienced medical device quality leader who builds strong teams, makes sound risk-based decisions and drives continuous improvement in a highly regulated, high-volume manufacturing environment at a global scale.
 
 
**Responsibilities**

* Lead, coach and develop a team of Quality Engineers; set priorities, manage workload and resourcing, conduct performance reviews and development plans, and lead hiring.
* Serve as Quality lead for the design transfer of new products and product design changes, ensuring quality deliverables (e.g. Project Quality Plans, Design Transfer Plans, Product Launch Plans) are created and properly executed through each phase gate.
* Serve as global process owner for Production & Process Controls and Design Transfer including procedure continuous improvement, performance monitoring of KPIs, and development of new or expanded processes to support Insulet’s growing production capacity.
* Support manufacturing process validation, equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and Test Method Validation for new manufacturing lines, capacity expansion, site transfers and equipment upgrades; review and approve plans, protocols and reports.
* Drive process risk management across all sites, including pFMEA governance and integration of nonconformance and production data into risk management.
* Lead remediation and compliance initiatives and provide Quality oversight of CAPAs, investigations, quality events and nonconformances, ensuring effective root cause analysis and verification of effectiveness.
* Partner with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers to deploy harmonized quality and process improvements.
* Provide Quality leadership for enterprise systems and digital initiatives (e.g. SAP, MES, eDHR, eQMS).
* Prepare and present quality metrics and project status for operations leadership, QMS process owner forums, and management review.
* Support internal and external audits as a subject matter expert, maintain inspection readiness, and serve as the escalation point for cross-functional quality questions from Operations, Engineering and Supply Chain.

**Education And Experience**

* BS degree in engineering, a technical or scientific discipline; and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Master's degree in engineering or technical or scientific discipline preferred.
* Minimum 10 years' experience in Medical Device Quality Assurance.
* 3-5 years' experience managing people, including leading engineers and technical staff.
* In-depth knowledge of FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485 and ISO 14971.
* Demonstrated experience leading design transfer and process validation for high-volume manufacturing of single-use products, preferably on automated manufacturing equipment.
* Experience with process risk management (pFMEA), CAPA, nonconformance and change control processes; QMS process ownership experience preferred.
* Experience with statistical methods (e.g. statistical process control, sampling plans, Test Method Validation, gauge R&R, and capability).
* Experience working with global manufacturing sites and contract manufacturers.
* Experience with eQMS/PLM, ERP and data visualization tools, as well as word processing, spreadsheet and database programs.

**Skills/Competencies**

* Proven ability to build, lead and develop high-performing teams, including effective delegation and succession planning.
* Strategic thinking with the ability to organize, judge and balance priorities across multiple complex projects.
* Sound, risk-based decision making in a highly regulated environment.
* Strong verbal (including presentation) and written communication skills, with the ability to influence and present to executive leadership.
* Effective collaboration and communication with individuals at multiple levels and across functions, sites and geographies.
* Strong problem solving / root cause analysis skills.
* Ability to generate and maintain organized and accurate records, and to follow up with task owners to close out open items.

**Other Expectations**

* Flexibility to work across multiple time zones, outside of normal working hours.
* Travel (International) – 10%

*NOTE: This position is eligible for hybrid working arrangements (requires on-site work from an Insulet office).*
**Additional Information**
Compensation & Benefits: For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $138,700.00 - $208,000.00 This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation. We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
 
 

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance

* Paid time off (PTO)

Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety Quality Assurance (FSQA)
new_roles.description:
**Purpose**
Dole Packaged Foods is a purpose led organization that is a champion of accessible fruit nutrition and builds a brighter future for people through the goodness of fruit.
 
 
At Dole, our culture is uniquely driven by core Values. Our commitment to these Values transforms our work into a meaningful journey toward a brighter future together. Here, you'll be part of a respectful, inclusive culture that deeply values our colleagues, customers, and global communities. We strive for excellence, empowering each other to confidently overcome challenges, continuously learn, and achieve world-class results. Guided by unwavering integrity, our actions consistently reflect our commitment to always doing what's right, fostering lasting trust and strong relationships. Through a spirit of collaboration, we cultivate positivity, generosity, and genuine teamwork, enabling collective success toward our One Dole Purpose. Our innovative spirit leads directly to meaningful outcomes and business success.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Regional Food Safety & Quality Assurance (FSQA) provides leadership and direction for food safety and quality across the North America region. Serving as a key partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership, this role oversees regional and site FSQA execution, drives performance and continuous improvement, and serves as a primary Quality representative for customers and key business partners.
 
 
Working collaboratively across Operations, Supply Chain and Global FSQR, the Senior Manager helps translate company priorities into effective execution while strengthening food safety and quality capability throughout the region. This is a highly visible leadership role for an experienced professional who enjoys developing people, solving complex problems and influencing how Quality supports the business.
 
 
This role provides flexibility to work in a hybrid environment of home and our Westlake Village, CA office. (Hybrid is defined as 3 times per week in the office).
 
 
**Responsibilities**
**Primary Accountabilities:**
**Regional FSQA Leadership & Execution**

* Lead food safety and quality execution across North America, providing oversight to regional and site FSQA teams and serving as the primary FSQA partner to regional business and Supply Chain leadership.
* Monitor significant food safety and quality risks, performance gaps and corrective actions, ensuring effective execution, follow-through and appropriate escalation.
* Lead, coach and develop FSQA personnel while strengthening food safety and quality culture, capability and accountability across the region.

**Program Deployment & Capability Building**

* Lead regional implementation and reinforcement of company food safety and quality programs, standards and requirements including training and capability building across applicable functions.
* Coordinate regional food safety and quality incidents, ensuring appropriate assessment, communication, escalation and corrective action in partnership with relevant stakeholders.
* Partner with Global FSQR subject-matter experts to address technical and capability needs and support development of regional or facility SOPs, protocols and other supporting documentation.

**Customer, Business & Supply Chain Partnership**

* Serve as the primary North America Quality Representative for customers including strategic customer relationships, audits, inquiries and quality-related issues.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Operations, Commercial, Procurement, R&D and other functions to integrate food safety and quality requirements into business activities, commercialization and change initiatives.
* Coordinate regional FSQA activities involving suppliers, third-party manufacturers, warehousing and transportation in partnership with the appropriate Global FSQR teams.

**Performance & Continuous Improvement**

* Drive regional FSQA performance through KPIs, scorecards, trend analysis and management reporting, providing appropriate visibility to regional leadership and Global FSQR.
* Identify systemic risks, recurring issues and improvement opportunities and drive effective corrective and preventive actions across the region.
* Manage regional FSQA resources and priorities to support business needs, strengthen execution and continuously improve food safety and quality performance.
* Other duties as assigned

**Qualifications**
**Experience, Knowledge, & Skills You Bring:**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in food safety, quality assurance or related food manufacturing disciplines, including demonstrated leadership responsibility.
* Strong knowledge of food safety and quality management systems, HACCP/Preventive Controls, GMPs, GFSI-recognized certification schemes and applicable U.S./Canada food regulations.
* Experience working across manufacturing, Supply Chain and cross-functional business environments.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence and work effectively across organizational boundaries.
* Experience managing customer quality relationships and communicating effectively with senior business leaders.
* Strong understanding of incident management, risk assessment, corrective and preventive action, and continuous improvement principles.
* Strong analytical and communication skills with the ability to translate technical issues and performance data into practical business actions.
* Demonstrated ability to coach and develop technical professionals and build effective cross-functional relationships.

**What You’ll Need to Succeed:**

* Passionate about a purpose driven career
* Committed to fostering inclusive environments that support employee development and well-being
* Sets clear expectations, encourages innovation, and drives continuous improvement
* Models and coaches towards transparency and integrity in decision-making
* Effectively facilitates cross-team communication and teamwork

**Education & Certification:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Biology, Chemistry or Life Sciences is required.
* Advanced degree preferred but not required.
* HACCP and/or Preventive Controls Qualified Individual (PCQI) training strongly preferred.
* Relevant GFSI, auditing, food safety or quality certifications are beneficial.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Ability to sit and use the computer for extended periods of time; ability to answer phones and use a variety of office equipment; ability to lift 15 pounds and reach overhead.

**Travel Requirements:**

* Approximately 30-40%, including travel to company facilities, customers, and business partners as required.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.**
**For Jobs Based In California**
Hiring Pay Scale: $145,000 to $170,000
 
 
Dole Packaged Foods is committed to paying our Associates fairly and equitably. The pay rate offered will consider a wide range of factors, including but not limited to experience, education, accomplishments, and location. Pay scales are subject to review on a regular basis and will be updated as appropriate.
