new_roles.title: Director Destination Care Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Summary and Responsibilities**

The Director of Destination Care Operations drives the day-to-day operational success of CommonSpirit Health’s destination care program in partnership with clinical, financial, and internal and external stakeholders – serving patients traveling 150 or more miles for specialty care, from neighboring communities across the United States to international markets. The Director advances program performance, team excellence, and a concierge-caliber patient experience, ensuring every patient experiences frictionless care from first inquiry through return home. This role is suited to a self-driven leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and brings strong team leadership, process improvement skills, and comfort leading teams through change. The ideal candidate leads with adaptability, resourcefulness, and a collaborative spirit, and is deeply committed to delivering an exceptional experience for every destination care patient. This is an in-person, onsite role.

* Oversees the day-to-day operational performance of the destination care program, ensuring consistent and high-quality service delivery across all phases of the patient journey. Oversees referral intake and coordination workflows, ensuring timely and accurate routing, follow-up, and communication with referring providers and patients.
* Ensures patients, families, and referring partners experience seamless, concierge-caliber service from initial contact through post-discharge follow-up; conducts regular patient and family rounding to assess experience, identify service gaps and recovery opportunities, reinforce service standards, and gather patient stories that reflect the destination care experience.
* Delivers and ensures culturally informed service, communication, and care coordination across diverse domestic and international patient populations. Partners with clinical leadership and clinical advisory resources to support patient care operations and ensure the clinical needs of the destination care population are addressed. Identifies and leads process improvement and workflow optimization initiatives to advance operational efficiency, service quality, and patient satisfaction; develops and maintains operational protocols and standards that support consistent program delivery.
* Establishes and maintains documentation standards and data integrity practices across the team to support accurate program reporting, operational decision-making, and continuity of patient care. Serves as the escalation point for the team and provides availability for complex or time-sensitive situations as they arise. Manages the destination care program budget and is accountable for financial performance against established targets.
* Sets clear performance expectations, invests in professional growth, and builds and sustains a high-performing team culture grounded in service excellence, operational consistency, and continuous improvement; establishes clear standards and ensures consistent adherence across the team, addressing performance gaps directly and constructively.
* Oversees onboarding, cross-training, and workflow consistency across the program. Leads change management efforts within the team to support adoption of new workflows, service standards, and program initiatives.

**Job Requirements**

Required

* Bachelors Other Bachelor’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, or a related field. and 5 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience managing and developing teams in a complex, matrixed healthcare organization, with direct accountability for program performance outcomes, upon hire and
* Experience delivering high-touch, patient-centered services for complex or high-acuity patient populations, including programs such as transplant, oncology, specialty referral, or equivalent tertiary or quaternary care settings, upon hire and
* Experience with electronic health record and hospital information systems; proficiency with productivity suites including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office., upon hire or

Preferred

* Masters Other Master’s degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Nursing, or a related field and 7-9 years 7 or more years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare or patient services operations, upon hire and
* Experience with international patient programs, embassy-sponsored care, or global sponsor coordination., upon hire and
* Clinical background including Registered Nurse (RN) licensure or equivalent clinical operations experience, upon hire and
* Experience in a dedicated destination care, international patient services, or specialty referral program at an academic medical center or large health system, upon hire and
* Experience building or expanding programs, including policy and operational protocol development, upon hire and
* Experience preparing and delivering financial and operating performance reports and presentations for leadership, upon hire and
* Experience with referral management, patient access, financial counseling, registration, or admissions workflows, upon hire and
* Experience managing program operations across multiple facilities or markets within a large health system., upon hire
* Certified Case Manager, upon hire or
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt Certification, upon hire or
* Project Management Professional, upon hire or
* Registered Nurse: TX, upon hire

Where You'll Work

Baylor St. Luke’s Medical Center is an 1,045 bed facility located in the Texas medical center. A joint venture with Baylor College of Medicine, Baylor St. Luke’s is an internationally recognized leader in research and clinical excellence that has given rise to breakthroughs in cardiovascular care, neuroscience, oncology, transplantation, and more. The hospital is home to the Dan L Duncan Comprehensive Cancer Center, a nationally-accredited and NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Our new McNair Campus is designed around the human experience—modeled on evidence-based practices for the safety of patients, visitors, staff, and physicians. The 27.5-acre campus represents the future of healthcare through a transformative alliance focused on leading-edge patient care, research, and education.

 **Pay Range** 
$60.24 - $89.60 /hour

identity_held_roles.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
**Overview**
Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.
 
 
**Compensation:**
$185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.
 
 
**Location:**
Dallas, TX
 
 
**Health Benefits**
Benefits of working for Primo Brands:
 
 
Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)
 
 
**Retirement/Investing**
401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
 
 
**Insurance**
Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment
 
 
**Other Great Benefits**
Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.
 
 
The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.
 
 
The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.
* Provide leadership oversight of quality management systems, audits, inspections, recalls, and corrective action processes.
* Promote a culture of first-time-right execution and continuous quality improvement.

**Financial & Productivity Performance**

* Own regional manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, conversion costs, and operating performance.
* Deliver annual productivity, cost savings, and efficiency targets.
* Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve OEE, optimize labor deployment, and improve asset performance.
* Partner with Finance to ensure operational results support annual business plans and long-range objectives.

**Talent & Organizational Leadership**

* Build and lead high-performing teams through effective leadership, coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
* Develop strong Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Technical Managers, Operations Managers, and functional leaders.
* Drive leadership capability, workforce planning, succession readiness, and organizational effectiveness.
* Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and associate engagement.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead implementation of manufacturing excellence initiatives across the region.
* Drive improvements in OEE, asset reliability, labor productivity, quality, and service performance.
* Leverage Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustainable results.
* Establish performance metrics and governance processes that accelerate operational excellence.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Contribute to the development and execution of Supply Chain and Manufacturing strategies.
* Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate network optimization opportunities, capacity investments, automation initiatives, and capital projects.
* Lead manufacturing integration, transformation, and change management initiatives.
* Support enterprise growth through scalable operational solutions and disciplined execution.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* Multiple manufacturing facilities within assigned region.
* Direct leadership of Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Regional Engineering, Manufacturing Excellence, and operational support functions.
* Accountability for regional safety, quality, production, service, cost, talent, and financial performance.
* Significant influence on capital planning, organizational design, and operational strategy.

**Qualifications**
**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or related field required.
* Master's Degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years leading multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing large-scale manufacturing networks in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or related industries.
* Proven success leading large teams through operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing significant P&L, productivity, and capital investment responsibilities.

**Skills & Competencies**

* Executive leadership and influence.
* Manufacturing operations expertise.
* Safety and quality systems leadership.
* Financial and operational acumen.
* Strategic thinking and execution.
* Change leadership and organizational transformation.
* Talent development and succession management.
* Data-driven decision making.
* Cross-functional collaboration.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

**Success Measures**

* Safety Performance
* Quality Compliance & Customer Metrics
* OEE and Asset Reliability
* Production Attainment
* Cost per Case Equivalent
* Labor Productivity
* Service Levels / OTIF
* Associate Engagement
* Leadership Bench Strength
* Productivity Savings Delivery
* Capital Project Execution
* Manufacturing Excellence Maturity

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**
**Salary Range Disclaimer**
The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.
 
 
Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill. At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.
 
 
Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.
 
 
Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

identity_held_roles.title: Vice President of Manufacturing (Automotive)
identity_held_roles.description:
Our client is a leading precision metal component manufacturer serving the automotive and industrial sectors. Operating multiple advanced manufacturing facilities across the United States, they specialize in high-volume production using advanced metal forming and stamping technologies. They supply critical components to tier-one automotive suppliers and industrial OEMs.

**The Role**

We are recruiting a Vice President of Manufacturing to lead manufacturing operations for a multi-facility U.S. operation. Reporting directly to the President, this role has responsibility for all manufacturing and quality departments at the primary facility and oversight of operations at additional locations. This is a high-impact position with significant visibility throughout the organization and the opportunity to shape operational strategy during a period of growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing and quality departments, ensuring optimal performance across production facilities
* Manage comprehensive capital and operational budgets with focus on balancing growth investments with financial discipline
* Establish manufacturing goals, performance metrics, and quality expectations
* Oversee staff recruitment and ensure proper staffing levels across all functional areas
* Maintain direct customer relationships regarding production capabilities, delivery schedules, and quality standards
* Implement and monitor continuous improvement initiatives to reduce costs and enhance efficiency
* Drive adoption of industry quality management systems (IATF, ISO TS 16949, ISO 14001)
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, and safety regulations across all operations
* Lead cross-functional initiatives and participate in strategic planning with the executive team
* Monitor production performance data and identify improvement opportunities

**Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, or related field

* 15 years of manufacturing experience, with at least 10 years in management or supervisory roles
* Demonstrated experience leading manufacturing operations in automotive or precision metal processing industries
* Strong background with metal stamping, forming, or similar high-volume production processes
* Proficiency with lean manufacturing methodologies and continuous improvement frameworks (5S, Kaizen, etc.)
* Experience managing quality systems and regulatory compliance (IATF, TS 16949 preferred)
* Proven ability to lead and develop teams
* Strong communication skills and collaborative leadership approach
* Experience managing P&L and capital budgets
* Travel: Approximately 10% per month (primarily to other company facilities)

**Preferred Qualifications**

* MBA or advanced degree in Business or Engineering
* Experience managing multi-facility operations
* Background with tool design or manufacturing process optimization
* Exposure to global manufacturing environments
* Experience navigating supply chain challenges in automotive manufacturing

**Benefits**

* Base Salary: $200,000 - $235,000

* Performance Bonus
* Comprehensive health insurance coverage
* 401(k) retirement plan

identity_held_roles.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing (Rubber)**

The Director of Manufacturing will oversee rubber production operations across 2 manufacturing plants with 200 total employees, 100 employees per plant, 1 union plant & 1 non-union, 5-8 Direct Reports (Department Managers) with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, and cost, acting as leader with accountability for both operations.

**Location**
: Columbia, Missouri (Relocation Assistance Offered)

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.
* Develop, standardize, and improve mixing programs (load order, ram pressure, rotor speed, mix time, dump temperature, energy-based and multi-stage mixing) for new and existing compounds, including EPDM, CR, HNBR, NBR, SBR, and NR systems.
* Oversee textile operations (cord unwinding, coating, and rewinding) and raw material handling, heating, and cooling to ensure consistent adhesion and reinforcement performance in finished belts and hoses.
* Lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, the materials lab, process and manufacturing engineers, and downstream operations, leading investigations through disciplined experimentation.
* Establish a single, controlled system of work instructions, batch cards, and process parameters across both sites so that the same compound is produced the same way regardless of site, shift, or operator.
* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

Mill: raw materials are received and handled, then weighed, mixed, heated, and cooled to produce uniform rubber compound for downstream product production.

Textiles: cord is carefully unwound, coated, and rewound to specification, giving finished products consistent strength and adhesion.

*Safety, Compliance & Culture*

* Champion a zero-harm safety culture, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mill nip and pinch-point hazards, hot surfaces, combustible dust, and chemical handling.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, SDS requirements, and applicable customer, ISO/IATF, and corporate standards.
* Drive 5S, standardized work, and lean manufacturing practices; treat housekeeping as both a safety and a quality requirement.
* Build a culture of accountability in which following the documented process is the standard and deviations are surfaced openly.

*Talent Development & Organizational Capability*

* Build a bench of operators, leads, supervisors, and managers through structured training, skills matrices, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and partner with HR on coaching, corrective action, recognition, and labor relations.
* Capture experienced operators' tribal knowledge and convert it to documented, teachable standards.
* Attract, hire, and retain top technical and operational talent in a competitive labor market.

*Strategy & Continuous Improvement*

* Work with the plant leadership and engineering leadership to define annual improvement initiatives, then align cross-functional teams to targets and track results.
* Lead capital projects, technology transfers, and new-process launches from concept through ramp-up.
* Use KPIs, trend charts, and daily management routines to drive visibility, problem solving, and sustained results.
* Contribute to the North American and global compounding strategy, sharing best practices with sister sites and corporate technology teams.

*Key Performance Indicators*

* Safety: recordable incident rate, near-miss reporting, and audit results
* Compound first-pass quality and out-of-spec rate; rheology capability and variation reduction
* Downstream molding and processing results attributable to compound and cord
* Schedule attainment and on-time delivery to downstream operations
* Scrap, rework, yield, and material and conversion cost versus budget
* Equipment uptime and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Operator qualification coverage and cross-training depth
* Employee engagement, turnover, and leadership bench strength

**Qualifications Seeking:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Polymer, Mechanical, Materials, or Industrial), Chemistry, or a related technical field preferred. Experience in lieu of Bachelors will be considered.
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 5–10 years of hands-on polymer or rubber compounding and mixing experience.
* 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing managers and multi-shift operations, including responsibility for safety, quality, cost, and delivery.
* Strong working knowledge of internal mixers (tangential and intermeshing), two-roll mills, TSE, weigh-up/batching, and compound testing (Mooney, MDR/RPA, specific gravity, dispersion).
* Demonstrated experience reducing process variation using DOE, SPC, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, lab, engineering, and production teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, direct without being abrasive.
* Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% between sites and to work on the floor in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications (Not Required):**

* Master's degree in Polymer Science, Chemistry, or Engineering, or an MBA.
* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems, mixing control software, and automation for production and material traceability.
* Experience leading capital projects, new-equipment commissioning, or greenfield/expansion launches.

**Core Competencies Seeking:**

* Technical depth: credible expert in rubber chemistry, rheology, and mixing who can coach engineers and operators alike.
* Leadership: develops managers, builds accountability, and engages a unionized or non-union frontline workforce.
* Systems thinking: standardizes work and builds sustainable processes rather than relying on individual heroics.
* Analytical rigor: makes decisions with data, experimentation, and clear trend visibility.
* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Production
identity_held_roles.description:
**About the Opportunity**

A well-established manufacturing organization in the aviation and aerospace industry is seeking an experienced
**Director of Production**
to oversee and improve its manufacturing operations.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone with direct aerospace or aviation manufacturing experience who can manage production activities, lead teams, improve operational efficiency, and ensure consistent product quality and on-time delivery.

The ideal candidate is a practical, floor-oriented leader who understands production planning, manufacturing processes, equipment maintenance, and resource management.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily manufacturing and production activities to ensure operational efficiency, product quality, and timely delivery.
* Manage production schedules, workflow, resource allocation, and manufacturing capacity.
* Lead and coordinate production planning and maintenance teams to maintain equipment reliability and operational continuity.
* Monitor production costs, operating expenses, and departmental budgets while identifying cost-saving opportunities.
* Establish and track KPIs related to productivity, production volume, quality, scrap rates, lead times, and on-time delivery.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing processes, reduce waste, and increase production capacity.
* Ensure compliance with aviation manufacturing standards, safety regulations, environmental requirements, and customer specifications.
* Work closely with department managers and supervisors to establish performance goals and maintain accountability.
* Coach, develop, and mentor production leaders and supervisors.
* Support facility improvements, equipment upgrades, capital projects, and the implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, teamwork, safety, and operational excellence.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent experience will also be considered.
* Approximately 8–10 years of progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Direct experience in
 **aviation or aerospace manufacturing operations is required**
 .
* Previous experience managing production teams, manufacturing schedules, and operational resources.
* Strong understanding of production planning, manufacturing processes, maintenance coordination, and quality control.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to improve productivity, control costs, and meet production targets.
* Strong leadership, problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* **Fluency in both English and Spanish (written and spoken) is required.**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working with ERP systems; Quantum experience is a plus.
* Six Sigma Green Belt certification or higher.
* Lean Manufacturing or other continuous improvement certifications.
* Experience managing manufacturing budgets and operational performance metrics.

**Ideal Candidate**

The successful candidate will be a hands-on production leader who is comfortable working directly with manufacturing teams and supervisors. This position is best suited for someone with a strong background in aerospace manufacturing who can balance people leadership with daily production execution and continuous improvement.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description**
As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
 
 
 
 
**Key Responsibilities Include**
**Strategic Product Stream Leadership**

* Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
* Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

**Program Execution**

* Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
* Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

**Performance Improvement**

* Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
* Implement metrics to monitor production performance
* Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances

**Required Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
* Minimum 10 years’ experience in production/manufacturing
* Minimum 6 years’ experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
* Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
* Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools

**Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Proficiency with Oracle ERP
* Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
* Minimum 10 years’ experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams

**Pay Information**
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
 
 
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
 
 
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
 
 
 
 
**About BAE Systems, Inc.**
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
 
 
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.
 
 
This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

identity_held_roles.description:
Job ID: 530933
 
 
Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.
 
 
To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com
 
 
\*\*Job Summary\*\*
 
 
The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.
 
 
\*\*Job Location\*\*
 
 

* This role will work out of our plant in Louisville, NE.

\*\*Job Responsibilities\*\*
 
 

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

\*\*Job Requirements\*\*
 
 

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

\*\*What CRH Offers You\*\*
 
 

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

\*\*About CRH\*\*
 
 
CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.
 
 
If you're up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!
 
 
Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.
 
 
EOE/Vet/Disability
 
 
CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
 
AI tools may be used in certain stages of the employment lifecycle, such as candidate review; however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.

identity_held_roles.description:
LHH is seeking a Plant Manager for a Direct Hire, Permanent Placement position with a manufacturing client located near Fort Wayne, IN. This is an opportunity to lead a growing manufacturing operation where you will have significant autonomy and direct influence over business and operational performance. You will join an existing team, provide guidance, drive business growth, and lead critical projects with key customers. The compensation is commensurate to experience and will range between $140,000–165,000 per year plus bonus and includes comprehensive benefit and insurance plans, generous Paid Time Off, and a 401K plan with a company match.

***\*\*\*Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.\*\*\****

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for across the manufacturing facility.
* Build an engaged, accountable culture through visible leadership, open communication, coaching, and employee development.
* Evaluate production performance and operating data to identify opportunities for efficiency, capacity, and cost improvements.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase productivity, reduce waste, and deliver measurable financial results.
* Manage staffing, training, labor utilization, production schedules, and resources to support changing business requirements.
* Review and improve operating procedures, standard work, and processes to strengthen consistency and accountability.
* Develop operating budgets and manage plant spending with a strong focus on profitability and cost control.
* Lead strategic planning activities and establish performance measures that support key organizational objectives.
* Direct capital investments and special projects from planning through implementation and performance validation.
* Improve equipment reliability, utilization, manufacturing capacity, and overall operational effectiveness.
* Maintain strong customer service while balancing production priorities, operating costs, and delivery expectations.
* Foster collaboration across departments and effectively lead employees with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and personalities.
* Maintain a strong safety culture and ensure operations comply with applicable workplace and regulatory requirements.
* Proactively identify operational risks, develop practical action plans, and follow initiatives through completion.
* Partner with technical and business leaders to support long-term growth and continuous operational improvement.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Bachelor Degree in Engineering, Business Management, Operations, or related field is preferred**
* **Minimum of 10+ years of leadership experience within a manufacturing facility is required**
* **Must have at least 5+ years of experience at the Plant Manager level**
* **Must have the ability to manage P&L, labor costs, scheduling, capacity, and capital expenditures**
* Must have experience with ERP/MRP systems and data-driven operational reporting
* Ideal candidates will have experience with Lean Manufacturing
* Strong communication, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* **Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.**

If you or someone in your network fit this profile and would like to apply for this Plant Manager position near Fort Wayne, IN then please submit your application alongside your resume using the link in this posting.

**Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled**

To read our Candidate Privacy Information Statement, which explains how we will use your information, please navigate to https://www.lhh.com/us/en/candidate-privacy

The Company will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with federal, state, and local laws and/or security clearance requirements, including, as applicable:

* The California Fair Chance Act
* Los Angeles City Fair Chance Ordinance
* Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers
* San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance

identity_held_roles.description:
**About The Position**
****Plant Manager at FRC, a Clarience Technologies Company****
****Location: Nesconset, NY****
****﻿****
****﻿New York Annual Salary Range: $145,000 - $175,000 USD****
****﻿****
Position Summary
 
 
****FRC****
, a Clarience Technologies company, is a leading manufacturer and innovator of firefighting and emergency response technologies serving fire apparatus OEMs, dealers, and fire departments throughout North America. FRC develops industry-leading solutions including fire apparatus controls, pressure governors, instrumentation, LED scene lighting, electronic control systems, and FoamPro® foam injection and proportioning systems.
 
 
The
****Plant Manager****
leads a manufacturing operation of approximately 80 employees across 2 shifts and is responsible for Production, Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, and Facilities. This role is accountable for driving a world-class safety culture, delivering revenue and profitability objectives, achieving quality and operational performance targets, and leading continuous improvement initiatives across the organization.
 
 
As a key member of the leadership team, the Plant Manager will develop and execute operational strategies that support growth, innovation, customer satisfaction, and operational excellence.
 
 
**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Safety Leadership
* Champion and drive a proactive safety culture.
* Ensure achievement of targeted safety metrics.
* Lead safety initiatives, investigations and corrective actions.
* Operational Leadership
* Lead Production, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities and Quality functions.
* Provide weekly revenue forecasts and operational updates.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen and continuous improvement efforts.
* Support new product introductions and manufacturing readiness.
* Financial Management
* Manage labor, variable overhead and fixed overhead costs.
* Achieve gross margin objectives and operational budgets.
* Lead cost reduction and productivity improvement initiatives.
* Quality Management
* Develop and implement the Quality Management System.
* Drive quality metrics, corrective actions and continuous improvement.
* Ensure customer quality requirements are achieved.
* Leadership and Talent Development
* Lead supervisors and functional managers.
* Develop organizational capability and succession plans.
* Partner with HR on employee development and workforce planning.

**Managerial Responsibilities**

* Directly manages departmental supervisors and functional leaders within Production, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, and Quality. Procurement and Scheduling report directly to the President and are not part of this role’s reporting structure.

****Competencies****

* Leadership and team development
* Financial and business acumen
* Operational excellence mindset
* Strong communication and influence skills
* Data-driven decision making
* Problem solving and continuous improvement
* Integrity, accountability and results orientation

*****﻿*****
**\*We do not discriminate in hiring or employment on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, marital status, national origin, sexual orientation, age, disability, ancestry veteran status or any other status protected by law.**
**Requirements**
****Education and Experience****

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, Business or related field preferred.
* 7-10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Experience managing revenue, labor, overhead and gross margin performance.
* Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement experience required.

**Computer Skills**

* ERP/MRP systems
* Microsoft Office Suite
* Manufacturing reporting tools
* Workforce/timekeeping systems

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager – Reman & Refurb Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
**Brief Description**
**Senior Manager – Reman & Refurb Operations**
**About The Role**
The Senior Manager – Reman & Refurb Operations leads the development, execution, and growth of SANY America’s component remanufacturing and full-machine refurbishment operations. This position oversees shop performance, safety, quality, cost, inventory, suppliers, and dealer support while building a scalable, profitable operation that improves machine uptime and lifecycle value.
 
 
With current revenues over $500 million, SANY America continues to make strong progress and significant investments in the Americas market; the organization is now pursuing an aggressive growth strategy and is looking to move quickly beyond this initial platform and increase their market share.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Business Strategy & Operations**

* Develop and execute the U.S. remanufacturing and refurbishment roadmap, including future certified refurbished equipment programs.
* Direct production planning, technician utilization, shop capacity, workflows, turnaround times, and performance standards.
* Build and coach technical and operations teams, establishing clear ownership, training, and accountability.

**Remanufacturing & Refurbishment**

* Standardize machine inspection, teardown, repair, component replacement, testing, cosmetic restoration, and final acceptance.
* Expand viable remanufacturing offerings for engines, hydraulics, powertrain, electronics, and other high-value assemblies.
* Establish documented repair procedures, quality gates, testing standards, failure analysis, and corrective actions.

**Financial & Inventory Management**

* Own operating budgets, rebuild costs, labor standards, margin performance, scrap reduction, and repair-versus-replace decisions.
* Develop core return, valuation, salvage, used-component, and reman inventory controls to improve recovery and reduce working capital.
* Track operational and financial KPIs, including cycle time, capacity, first-pass quality, revenue, and profitability.

**Suppliers, Dealers & Cross-Functional Support**

* Manage outside rebuild suppliers and technical partners against quality, cost, warranty, and lead-time expectations.
* Partner with Service, Parts, Warranty, Product, Sales, Finance, and dealers to support customer uptime and refurbishment opportunities.
* Support certified refurbished equipment programs through condition grading, inspection documentation, and warranty coordination.

**Safety & Continuous Improvement**

* Maintain a safe, organized, compliant shop with appropriate PPE, equipment controls, and safe work practices.
* Implement Lean, 5S, standard work, visual management, root cause analysis, and ongoing process improvements.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered.
* 12+ years of progressive experience in remanufacturing, refurbishment, heavy equipment, automotive, industrial manufacturing, service operations, or a related field.
* 6+ years of direct people-management or operations-leadership experience.
* Strong understanding of engines, hydraulics, powertrain, electrical systems, and heavy equipment troubleshooting.
* Proven ability to manage production, quality, inventory, capacity, costs, KPIs, and financial performance.
* Strong communication, problem-solving, cross-functional leadership, and analytical skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience launching or expanding remanufacturing, machine rebuild, refurbishment, or certified pre-owned operations.
* Construction or off-highway equipment experience, including supplier and third-party rebuild partner management.
* Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, ERP, inventory, service, and warranty system experience.

**Work Environment & Physical Requirements**
**OFFICE + OPERATIONS WORK ENVIRONMENT**
This role is primarily office-based with regular work in remanufacturing, refurbishment, and equipment service areas. Duties may involve extended computer use, standing, walking, and observing or inspecting heavy machinery, tools, and shop operations. Exposure to noise, moving equipment, and varying temperatures may occur. Required personal protective equipment (PPE) must be worn in designated areas, with or without reasonable accommodation.
 
 
**Travel Requirements**
Occasional travel to SANY facilities, suppliers, dealers, and customer sites as business needs require.
 
 
**Compensation & Benefits**
Compensation will be competitive and commensurate with experience.
 
 

* Medical, dental, and vision
* Paid Time Off
* 401(k) savings plans
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)
* Company paid STD and LTD benefits
* Life Insurance
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT**
SANY America is an Equal Opportunity Employer and considers all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected status under applicable federal, state, or local law.
 
 
**DRUG AND ALCOHOL-FREE WORKPLACE NOTICE**
SANY America is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a drug and alcohol-free workplace consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Applicants may be required to complete pre-employment screenings, including drug and/or alcohol testing, as a condition of employment where permitted by applicable law. Testing requirements, employment practices, and workplace policies may vary based on work location, position responsibilities, business necessity, workplace safety considerations, customer requirements, contractual obligations, and applicable regulatory standards.
 
 
SANY America complies with applicable federal, state, and local laws relating to marijuana/cannabis use, including applicable medical and recreational marijuana laws where permitted. However, applicants and employees are prohibited from being impaired or under the influence of alcohol, illegal drugs, or other prohibited substances while working, operating Company vehicles or equipment, performing safety sensitive duties, conducting Company business, or while on Company property, consistent with applicable law.
 
 
Certain positions may be designated as safety sensitive or subject to additional regulatory, customer, contractual, operational, or workplace safety requirements and may require participation in pre-employment, random, reasonable suspicion, post-accident, return to duty, follow up, or other drug and/or alcohol testing programs in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr Manager of Manufacturing Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Company And Opportunity Overview**

WNA’s vision is to be a leading entrepreneurial player in terms of market share, agility, and game-changing solutions. WNA is a solution provider, creating value along the supply chain of our customers, from online purchase to their customers.

WNA is headquartered in the Charlotte Metro Area, North Carolina. With around 500 employees and ~$200M of sales, WNA focuses on the retail and distribution market segments with marquee customers such as Walmart, Amazon, and the majority of large grocers and retailers.

In addition to being the largest manufacturer of shopping carts in North America, WNA has three additional main product segments as well as a Service business, providing turnkey solutions for customer guidance (Access Systems), Shelving & Fixtures, and Material Handling products.

Access Solutions provides sophisticated customer guidance and loss prevention systems for major retailers. With German-engineered products and a strong installed base, this segment focuses on protecting existing market share while expanding into adjacent opportunities in smart retail, autonomous store technology, and digital integration.

Additionally, WNA offers a range of digital solutions integrated into our products, including advanced shopping cart containment systems, smart exit gate technology, and innovations for autonomous and semi-autonomous retail stores. We are continuously expanding and enhancing our digital offerings to meet evolving customer needs and drive industry advancement.

WNA is part of the Wanzl Group, headquartered in Germany, and has 12 plants in 8 countries, providing comprehensive, solutions-driven service and expert knowledge of local markets for customers across the globe through their 360° service.

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Manage a team of 5-10 Engineers, CAD Designers, & Engineering Technicians
* Drive LEAN implementation / LEAN transformation.
* Recommend and manage capital projects from concept through appropriation process, to project management and implementation for current production improvement.
* Select, develop, and train the Manufacturing Engineering Team
* Provide needed technical support and lead shop floor problem solving using world-class problem-solving methodologies.
* Create and maintain shop floor layouts, fostering material flow optimization.
* Creating and maintaining Manufacturing BOMs and Routings in ERP system
* Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) driven by R&D
* Support Industrialization in developing & implementing new production methods/processes.
* Process Capability Studies
* Standard Work Analysis, for both Direct and Indirect Labor
* Create test protocols, document and track results.
* Support for Operations, support for Tooling and Maintenance, Look for Efficiency Projects to increase Capacity, OEE, Reduce costs (Labor, Material, OH, etc.) and drive projects in consequence, review PMs, Cycle Times analysis, Downtime analysis.
* Develop Set-up technicians.

**Skills And Experience**

* BS in Engineering from an accredited university
* Minimum of 5 years engineering experience in a Manufacturing Environment, Design/R&D, & demonstrated engineering project leadership experience.
* LEAN and Six Sigma training preferred.
* Experience implementing LEAN Manufacturing projects.
* Proficient in use of software - CAD (SolidWorks), MS Project, MS Office, etc.
* Strong problem solving / analytical skills including identifying potential problems and developing effective solutions.
* Demonstrated Leadership skills.
* Minimal travel

identity_held_roles.description:
**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .
