existing_roles.description:
**Description**
Title: Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
  
  
Department: EHSQ / Quality
  
  
Location: Houston, TX
  
  
Supervisor: Sr. Director of Quality
  
  
Direct Reports: None
  
  
FLSA Status: Exempt
  
  
Position Status: Permanent, Full-time
  
  
Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Remote
  
  
Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS)
  
  
Hanwha Qcells USA Corp (“HQC US”) develops, invests, and delivers solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) projects through Engineering, Procurement, Construction (EPC) services in North America.
  
  
The company brings a decade of global leadership in solar PV to deliver utility-scale power generation plants customized for local and regional energy markets. HQC US offers the full spectrum of PV solutions – from the core technology of cells and modules to large-scale project development and investment. With proven capabilities across the solar and battery storage chain, HQC US minimizes uncertainty and risk, and helps customers achieve a higher return on their investment in renewable energy.
  
  
**Summary**
The Sr. Manager, Quality SME (BESS) (“Quality SME”) serves as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) construction. The Quality SME is responsible for developing and maintaining the processes, systems, Inspection & Test Plan (ITP) templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, and Standard Work Instructions (SWIs) that govern how Quality is planned, executed, and documented on BESS scopes, whether self-performed or subcontracted. The role covers both standalone BESS facilities and BESS integrated with utility-scale solar PV projects.
  
  
The Quality SME works alongside the Regional Quality Managers on every project with active BESS construction, integrating discipline requirements into the project Quality program and providing technical direction to the Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors hired for these scopes. Those personnel report to the assigned Site Quality Manager or Sr. Site Quality Manager, who remains the single point of contact and the ranking Quality authority on site. The Quality SME holds a matrixed line of technical direction to the discipline team, participates in hiring, onboarding, training, and performance input, and is accountable for the technical consistency, process discipline, and record integrity of BESS Quality across the portfolio.
  
  
Success in this role requires deep practical knowledge of utility-scale BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, power conversion systems (PCS) and inverters, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary power, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection, suppression, gas detection, and explosion control installation interfaces. Equally important is a working command of manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements, which often govern acceptance more directly than the project drawings. The Quality SME aligns closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to integrate Quality early and resolve technical questions consistently. Design interpretation, battery management and energy management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing remain with Engineering, Commissioning, and the manufacturer; the Quality SME ensures those interfaces are defined, documented, and respected.
  
  
This position reports directly to the Senior Director of Quality (or another designated member of senior management). The role is remote, with standard business hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. local time, or as site construction hours dictate during jobsite visits. Travel is required up to 50% of the time, which includes scheduled jobsite visits for oversight and technical authority, as well as short-notice trips and extended site visits as business needs dictate.
  
  
**Essential Job Function & Responsibilities**

* Serve as the company’s subject matter expert and technical authority for Quality on standalone and PV-integrated BESS construction, supporting the Senior Director of Quality and the Regional Quality Managers.
* Develop, own, and maintain company-standard ITP templates, Quality Control Verification Checklists, SWIs, and Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) content for BESS scopes, ensuring they reflect current engineering standards, manufacturer requirements, and lessons learned.
* Build and maintain BESS inspection templates and workflows in Procore, in coordination with Quality Systems, so that discipline inspections are performed and recorded consistently across all projects.
* Integrate with the assigned Regional Quality Manager on each project containing BESS scope, from pre-mobilization planning through turnover, confirming discipline requirements are incorporated into the Site-Specific Quality Management Plan (SSQMP), ITPs, inspection staffing plan, and inspection schedule.
* Support the Preconstruction Quality SME by tailoring discipline ITPs and checklists for project kickoff packages and identifying BESS-specific contract, manufacturer, testing, and authority having jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements.
* Provide technical direction to the BESS Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors assigned to projects, in coordination with the Site Quality Manager, who retains administrative supervision and day-to-day site direction.
* Participate in recruitment, technical interviewing, onboarding, and qualification of discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, and provide performance input to the Site Quality Manager and Regional Quality Manager.
* Develop and deliver discipline-specific training for Quality personnel, covering acceptance criteria, inspection methods, manufacturer requirements, documentation requirements, and common BESS failure modes.
* Conduct scheduled jobsite visits to verify implementation of the BESS Quality program, perform surveillance of field inspection activities, and audit discipline records in Procore for accuracy, completeness, traceability, and objective evidence.
* Provide technical review and approval of subcontractor Quality Control Plans, ITPs, and inspection forms for BESS scopes prior to acceptance by the Site Quality Manager, and verify subcontractor Quality performance through surveillance and audit.
* Provide technical review and concurrence on proposed repair and use-as-is dispositions for nonconformances within the discipline, and on other dispositions as requested by the Site Quality Manager, in coordination with Engineering and the manufacturer.
* Lead or support root cause analysis for significant or recurring BESS nonconformances, and drive corrective and preventive actions to closure across the portfolio.
* Exercise stop-work authority for quality-driven conditions in accordance with company policy, coordinating through the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact on site.
* Elevate unresolved technical disagreements with site Quality, Construction, subcontractor, or manufacturer personnel to the Regional Quality Manager and Senior Director of Quality, with a documented position and recommended resolution.
* Define Quality’s verification requirements for receiving, storage, preservation, handling, and installation of BESS equipment, including manufacturer limits on storage conditions, storage duration, and state-of-charge maintenance that affect product conformity and warranty.
* Verify that manufacturer installation checklists, field service requirements, and warranty-related documentation are integrated into ITPs and completed in sequence, and coordinate Quality activities with manufacturer field representatives.
* Review pre-commissioning and construction test records, including torque verification, insulation resistance, and continuity testing, for completeness and conformance with project specifications, manufacturer requirements, and ANSI/NETA ATS where applicable.
* Define and support Quality’s responsibilities within the functional testing and cold commissioning RACI and in mechanical completion, energization-readiness, and turnover verification for BESS systems, while maintaining clear separation from battery management system configuration, functional commissioning, and capacity testing responsibilities.
* Where required by contract and as directed by the Senior Director of Quality, support factory acceptance test (FAT) witnessing and source inspection of BESS enclosures, PCS, and transformers, and contribute to the development of a formal source inspection program as the organization establishes one.
* Coordinate with owner’s engineers, independent engineers, AHJs, fire officials, and third-party agencies on BESS Quality matters, including inspection and documentation requirements associated with fire and life-safety systems.
* Align closely with the Engineering and BESS teams to resolve technical questions, participate in design and constructability reviews, and maintain consistent acceptance criteria across projects and manufacturers.
* Monitor BESS Quality KPIs and nonconformance trends across the portfolio, and report findings, emerging risks, and recommendations to the Senior Director of Quality.
* Provide input on discipline staffing and resource planning, including the number and qualification of Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors and third-party testing needs, for estimating and project staffing plans.
* Define the BESS Quality records required for turnover and verify completeness of discipline turnover documentation, including manufacturer and warranty records.
* Capture lessons learned from executed projects and incorporate them into discipline templates, training, and the broader Quality Management System (QMS).
* Interact and collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, BESS, Construction, Commissioning, Subcontract Management, and Safety teams to embed Quality into project execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects, as assigned.
* Travel is required up to 50%, including scheduled jobsite visits, extended site visits, short-notice trips, and overnight stays.

**Key Competencies / Core Skills**

* Recognized technical authority who guides others through credibility and clear reasoning rather than positional authority.
* Translates engineering, manufacturer, code, and contract requirements into clear, inspectable acceptance criteria.
* Builds standardized tools, including ITPs, checklists, SWIs, and Procore templates, that scale across projects, manufacturers, and delivery models.
* Leads effectively within a matrixed structure, supporting the Site Quality Manager as the single point of contact while holding the technical standard for the discipline.
* Holds the standard under schedule and commercial pressure while maintaining professional, collaborative working relationships with project teams and manufacturers.
* Understands the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, manufacturer responsibilities, and Commissioning, and escalates appropriately.
* Maintains exceptional attention to detail across inspection records, preservation records, test reports, and supporting objective evidence.
* Analyzes deficiency trends across the portfolio and translates findings into durable process change.
* Communicates clearly and factually with field personnel, engineers, manufacturers, owners, AHJs, and executive leadership, both in writing and in person.
* Coaches and develops discipline Quality Field Leads and Quality Inspectors, treating development of the bench as a core responsibility.
* Manages multiple concurrent projects, travel demands, and shifting priorities while maintaining accountability.
* Maintains composure and a solutions-focused approach under pressure, disagreement, and challenging field conditions.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive quality experience in utility-scale renewable-energy, utility, or industrial construction, including at least 5 years of direct Quality responsibility on utility-scale BESS projects; utility-scale PV experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
* At least 5 years in a quality leadership or management role, including directing inspection personnel or leading Quality programs across multiple projects.
* Demonstrated experience authoring and maintaining ITPs, Quality Inspection Checklists, Standard Work Instructions, and procedures for BESS construction.
* Strong working knowledge of BESS construction, including equipment foundations and anchorage, battery enclosures and containers, PCS and inverter equipment, medium-voltage transformers, auxiliary systems, DC and AC cabling and terminations, grounding and bonding, thermal management systems, and fire detection and suppression installation interfaces.
* Demonstrated experience applying manufacturer-specific installation, preservation, and warranty requirements for utility-scale energy storage equipment.
* Demonstrated ability to read and apply IFC drawings, single-line diagrams, equipment layouts, grounding plans, cable schedules, specifications, approved submittals, and manufacturer installation manuals.
* Experience overseeing Quality on both self-performed and subcontracted BESS work, including review of subcontractor Quality Control Plans and ITPs.
* Experience coordinating Quality activities with manufacturer field representatives, owner’s engineers, independent engineers, testing agencies, and AHJs.
* Demonstrated experience with nonconformance management, root cause analysis methodology (5-Why, fishbone, fault tree, or equivalent), and corrective action programs.
* Demonstrated understanding of the boundaries between construction Quality, Engineering, manufacturer, and Commissioning responsibilities.
* Proficiency with Procore (Quality & Field Management modules) and SharePoint.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
* Ability to work remotely with a reliable high-speed internet connection and flexibility to support projects across Eastern through Pacific Time Zones as required.
* Must hold and maintain a valid U.S. driver’s license and have the ability to safely operate a motor vehicle, including the ability to rent vehicles for business travel without restrictions that would interfere with job performance.
* Ability to successfully pass a motor vehicle/driving record background check in accordance with company policy.
* Must be able to pass pre-employment, regular, and random drug and alcohol screenings in compliance with company and customer requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Engineering Technology, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline.
* Professional certifications such as:

+ American Society for Quality (ASQ): Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Construction Quality Manager (CCQM), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA)
+ North American Board of Certified Energy Practitioners (NABCEP): Energy Storage Installation Professional (ESIP) or PV Installation Professional (PVIP)
+ InterNational Electrical Testing Association (NETA): NETA Certified Technician, Level III or Level IV
+ Manufacturer credentials: Installation or field service certification on one or more utility-scale BESS platforms
+ Electrical licensing: State journeyman or master electrician license
+ Project Management Institute (PMI): Project Management Professional (PMP)

* Experience witnessing factory acceptance testing or performing source inspection of BESS enclosures, PCS, or transformers.
* Experience across multiple BESS manufacturers, battery technologies, PCS platforms, thermal management designs, and both AC-coupled and DC-coupled configurations.
* Working knowledge of NFPA 855, NEC (NFPA 70) Article 706, UL 9540 and UL 9540A, and the energy storage provisions of the International Fire Code.
* Experience supporting BESS mechanical completion, construction completion, or commissioning-readiness documentation.
* Working knowledge of ISO 9001 and formal Quality Management System requirements.
* Experience developing and delivering technical training for Quality or field personnel.
* Advanced proficiency with Procore, including inspection template configuration, reporting, and workflow design, as well as Power BI.
* Experience supporting utility-scale solar PV, medium-voltage collection, or substation scopes adjacent to BESS installations.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish, with the ability to communicate effectively across diverse project teams.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS
  
  

* Ability to remain in a stationary position for extended periods while operating a computer and reviewing documentation, drawings, and test records.
* Ability to effectively exchange accurate information in verbal and written form with employees, contractors, manufacturers, and external stakeholders.
* Ability to conduct regular jobsite visits requiring extended standing and walking on uneven or unpaved terrain, as well as bending, stooping, kneeling, and climbing stairs or ladders to access BESS enclosures and equipment areas.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds of inspection equipment, documentation, or other work-related materials as required.
* Ability to perform field activities while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility clothing, safety footwear, and arc-rated clothing or other project-specific PPE where required.
* Ability to safely access BESS and electrical construction areas in accordance with site safety requirements, electrical safe-work practices, BESS-specific hazard controls, and access controls.
* Ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time, including by air, with flexibility for short-notice trips, overnight stays, and extended site visits.
* Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
  
  

* Work is divided between a remote/home office environment, requiring reliable high-speed internet and standard office equipment, including audio/video conferencing, and active construction sites.
* Field work is performed at utility-scale BESS, solar, and substation construction sites, where conditions may include outdoor weather exposure, dust, moderate to high noise levels, moving construction equipment, and uneven terrain. Appropriate PPE will be provided and required.
* Field work regularly occurs in proximity to energized or potentially energized equipment and stored-energy hazards as projects progress toward energization, requiring strict adherence to electrical safety requirements, BESS hazard controls, and access controls.
* Work schedules during jobsite visits may vary based on construction activities, manufacturer availability, testing schedules, and project milestones, and may include early starts, extended hours, or weekends.
* Regular interaction with cross-functional teams in both virtual and in-person settings, requiring adaptability to both independent and collaborative work environments.

existing_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Engineering — Autonomous Airpower
existing_roles.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
  
  
**About The Team**
The Air Dominance and Strike Division is one of Anduril's fastest growing, most technically complex divisions. We develop and build collaborative combat aircraft, missiles, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. We are scaling production of autonomous aircraft across our manufacturing facilities. Manufacturing Engineering drives process development, production readiness, and the transition from prototype to rate — ensuring that what Design engineers create can be built reliably, repeatedly, and at scale.
  
  
**About The Job**
Anduril is seeking a Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering to lead ME strategy and execution across the Autonomous Airpower portfolio. This is not a single-program role — you will be the manufacturing engineering voice across every aircraft program in the portfolio, from early concept through full-rate production. You will work directly with chief engineers, program managers, and the growth team to shape what gets built, how it gets built, and whether it can be built on cost and on schedule.
  
  
You are the first person from the ME organization that program managers and growth leads turn to when evaluating emerging capabilities. You provide the manufacturing perspective on what is realistic and achievable — grounding engineering ambitions in production reality. You understand every phase of the aircraft lifecycle: DFM input during design, participation in design reviews, prototype and first-article builds, LRIP standup, and the transition to full-rate production. You know what it takes to go from a clean-sheet aircraft concept to hardware rolling off a production line.
  
  
You will build and lead a team of manufacturing engineers, set the technical direction for the ME organization, and represent manufacturing engineering to directors and executives. This role requires someone who has lived aircraft manufacturing — not managed it from a distance — and who can move fluidly between a factory floor conversation and an executive review.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead manufacturing engineering strategy and execution across the full Autonomous Airpower portfolio, spanning multiple aircraft programs in various stages of maturity
* Serve as the primary ME point of contact for program managers and the growth team on emerging capabilities — providing early-stage assessments of manufacturability, cost, schedule, and production feasibility
* Partner with chief engineers and design leadership during all phases of engineering development, from concept trades and DFM input through design reviews, prototype builds, LRIP, and full-rate production
* Build, develop, and lead a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers across disciplines — structures, mechanical systems, fluid systems, propulsion, avionics, and harnessing
* Drive cross-functional alignment between engineering, supply chain, manufacturing operations, program management, quality, and leadership to ensure production readiness across programs
* Own the ME cost and schedule position for your portfolio — developing estimates, tracking execution, identifying risks, and presenting status to directors and executives
* Represent manufacturing engineering in executive reviews, program gate reviews, and customer-facing discussions, translating production realities into clear, actionable information for senior leadership
* Establish manufacturing engineering standards, processes, and best practices that scale across programs and production sites
* Evaluate and advise on make-vs-buy decisions, capital investments, and production strategies based on deep knowledge of aircraft manufacturing capabilities and constraints
* Drive production readiness across the portfolio — MBOMs, process maturity, tooling readiness, rate-readiness assessments — ensuring programs are set up to succeed at each production milestone

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering
* 12+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace or defense, with significant time spent on aircraft programs
* Deep, hands-on knowledge of aircraft manufacturing across multiple disciplines — structures/composites, mechanical systems, fluid systems, avionics, harnessing, or propulsion
* Experience across the full aircraft production lifecycle: DFM, design reviews, prototype/first-article builds, LRIP, and full-rate production
* 5+ years of experience leading and developing manufacturing engineering teams
* Demonstrated ability to assess emerging programs and provide credible manufacturing cost, schedule, and feasibility inputs
* Experience presenting manufacturing status, risks, and recommendations to director-level and executive audiences
* Strong cross-functional leadership — proven ability to drive alignment across engineering, operations, supply chain, program management, and business leadership
* Experience managing manufacturing engineering budgets and cost positions across multiple programs
* Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience standing up new aircraft production lines from scratch — from facility planning through rate production
* Experience working directly with growth or business development teams to shape proposals and production strategies for new aircraft programs
* Experience with autonomous aircraft, UAV, or advanced air vehicle programs
* Knowledge of EVMS, earned value reporting, and program control fundamentals
* Experience with Manufacturing Readiness Levels (MRL) and Manufacturing Readiness Assessments (MRA)
* Experience working with Teamcenter, SAP, Oracle, or similar PLM/ERP platforms
* Master's degree in Engineering, Business, or related field
* Active U.S. Secret security clearance

US Salary Range
  
  
$183,000—$243,000 USD
  
  
**Benefits**
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
  
  
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.
*For more information, Explore Our Benefits.*
**Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams**
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
  
  
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
  
  

* No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
* Please always verify communications:

+ Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
+ Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

* Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
* What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

**Data Privacy**
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
  
  
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

existing_roles.description:
**Fantastic challenges. Amazing opportunities.**
GKN Aerospace is reimagining air travel: going further, faster and greener! Fuelled by great people whose expertise and creativity sets the standards in our industry, we’re inspired by the opportunities to innovate and break boundaries. We’re proud to play a part in protecting the world’s democracies. And we’re committed to putting sustainability at the centre of everything we do, opening up and protecting our planet. With over 16,000 employees across 32 manufacturing sites in 12 countries we serve over 90% of the world’s aircraft and engine manufacturers and achieved sales of £3.6bn in 2025. There are no limits to where you can take your career.
  
  
Role Summary
  
  
As part of GKN Aerospace Airframes E&T, Chief Manufacturing Engineers (CME) lead the development, industrialisation and improvement of Manufacturing Systems whilst serving as the customer-facing representatives of the ME function.
  
  
Day-to-day, a CME is focused on delivery of non-recurring engineering projects including New Product Introductions (NPI), Transfers of Work (ToW), Major Modifications (Mods), Technology Insertions and resolving manufacturing process related quality and delivery challenges together with production engineering teams.
  
  
When necessary, a CME may lead deployed ME resources to deliver these projects, ensuring compliance with identified requirements (e.g. Produceability, Productivity, Cost, Schedule, Regulatory) and adherence to Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) standards.
  
  
**Remote Role**
Travel Requirements
  
  
This is a remote working position that requires frequent routine and occasional non-routine travel (up to 25-50%) to be on-site at GKN facilities and suppliers, including but not limited to; Phoenix (AZ), Wichita (KS), Sumner (WA), Chihuahua (Mexico), Tallassee (AL).
  
  
Candidates must live in a location with strong transport links. This could be 1-2 hours drive (approx.) from a major international hub airport (e.g. Dallas, Atlanta, Houston) or locally to a regional airport with multiple flights per day to major hub airports.
  
  
Role Accountabilities
  
  

* Bids– Accountable to validate and approve the proposed definition of the Manufacturing System and its associated performance targets which are submitted at LG3 (Programme Launch). Working closely with the Industrial Architect, the CME reviews output for technical risks and communicates these to the Programme. This may include process flow, bill of materials, proposed industrial setting, product cost estimates, requirements compliance or technology developments needed. The CME owns the Non-Recurring Engineering cost estimate for the ME technical content delivery.
* NPI– Accountable for delivering a Manufacturing System that fulfils all agreed stakeholder requirements (technical, quality, regulatory), business case metrics and system performance targets between LG3 (Programme Launch) and LG7 (Steady State Production) whilst ensuring that planning, development and commissioning is completed on-schedule and on-cost.
* Sustaining – Accountable for the governance and oversight of a portfolio of Manufacturing Systems, delivered through regular review of system KPIs and Industrial Review assessments. Takes corrective action to ensure Manufacturing Systems continue to perform in-line with the productivity & quality targets set.
* Leadership of Projects- Accountable for delivery of the non-recurring ME activities within a given programme or project. Responsible to provide technical leadership and direction using project management fundamentals: planning & estimating, resourcing & budgeting and reporting on project performance (earned value) to internal business standards.
* Leadership of Teams – Accountable to the Programme and Site for effective utilisation of deployed manufacturing engineering resource while delivering ME content of projects by providing day-to-day coordination, recognition and accountability and implementing ME best practice with the deployed team.
* Quality – Accountable for delivery of manufacturing systems that are Zero Defect Manufacturing (ZDM) capable through a relentless focus on delivering APQP to the AS9145 standard during the NPI phase. Must exhibit and drive a product quality mind-set within ME and ensure compliance to agreed Customer, Regulatory, Business and functional standards.
* Relationships – Accountable to maintain positive and functional working relationships with internal and external customers, to communicate and inform clearly and frequently with key stakeholders within the business, and to foster and champion GKN’s 5 principles within sphere of influence.

**Required**
Role Qualifications
  
  

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional qualification in Engineering (Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials, Electrical, Chemical, or related discipline).
* Minimum of 8 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing or similar, highly regulated environments operating under AS9100 Quality Management Systems.
* Recent experience developing a manufacturing system for a New Product Introduction (NPI) with a comprehensive understanding of product lifecycle gate processes.
* Broad, hands-on experience with common manufacturing processes (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).
* Knowledgeable of structured problem solving and RCCA methodologies (e.g. 8D) and how to apply these to complex problems.
* Demonstrated capability to organise and drive technical projects to achieve business goals, preferably in complex multi-site environments.
* Ability to lead and influence people, build trust and establish effective working relationships within a global organisation and with external customer stakeholders.
* Fluent in English language, both written and spoken.
* US Person for Export Control purposes

**Preferred**

* Demonstrated deployment of AS9145 APQP process.
* Working knowledge of digital systems for manufacturing (PLM, MES, ERP).
* Deep, expert knowledge in one or more manufacturing process areas (e.g. machining, forming, welding, composites, assembly, metrology).

existing_roles.description:
**Job Description**
The Director PMO NPI/NPD is responsible for leading the successful transition of new products from R&D into scalable volume manufacturing. Sitting within the PMO and reporting to the VP of Production Engineering and Continuous Improvement (PECI), this role owns NPI execution, manufacturing readiness, and phase-gate milestone delivery across the product portfolio. The Director partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management to ensure products transition seamlessly into volume manufacturing — meeting customer, quality, cost, and delivery expectations — while building the processes, tooling, and team capabilities needed to scale.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**New Product Development & Launch**

* Own PLM milestone tracking, phase-gate execution, and portfolio pipeline alignment to ensure timely and effective product launches
* Drive product commercialization from R&D handoff through launch, ensuring new products meet or exceed customer, quality, cost, and delivery requirements
* Align cross-functionally on the new product pipeline and launch readiness across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management

**Manufacturing Readiness & Scale-Up**

* Lead the transition of products from R&D into volume manufacturing, establishing scalable and repeatable production processes
* Develop and ramp manufacturing capability and capacity for new products at the R&D site
* Establish and continuously improve the R&D production line to support prototype and pilot builds

**Automation, Tooling & Test**

* Lead automation initiatives including tooling, test fixtures, and production test requirement definition
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to ensure test and tooling solutions are scalable for volume production

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of Technical Program Managers and the Engineering Manager for Prototype and Pilot Builds
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement within the NPD PMO function

**Skill & Abilities**
**Ownership & Accountability**
Ability to drive NPI program outcomes from R&D handoff through volume manufacturing launch. Holds themselves and their team to commitments, drives decisions, and escalates risks proactively — ensuring programs stay on track.
  
  
**Program & Portfolio Management**
Ability to manage multiple NPI programs simultaneously across the portfolio, maintaining phase-gate discipline, milestone ownership, and pipeline visibility from commercialization through volume launch.
  
  
**Commercialization & NPI Execution**
Ability to take products through the commercialization phase — from R&D handoff to volume manufacturing — on time and within cost, quality, and delivery targets.
  
  
**Manufacturing & Production Readiness**
Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, scale-up requirements, tooling, automation, and test development — with the ability to translate R&D outputs into production-ready solutions.
  
  
**Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence**
Ability to align and drive execution across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management without direct authority over all stakeholders — critical in a PMO structure.
  
  
**Strategic Thinking & Prioritization**
Ability to manage competing program priorities at the portfolio level, make sound trade-off decisions, and keep initiatives aligned to business objectives.
  
  
**Team Development**
Ability to lead, develop and effectively scale a team to ensure the right capabilities and resourcing are in place at the right time.
  
  
**Stakeholder Communication & Reporting**
Ability to synthesize program status, risks, and decisions into clear, concise communication for senior leadership and the c-suite.
  
  
**Travel**
Ability to travel 10-20%
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field
* 15+ years of program management experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment, with a focus on new product introduction (NPI), product transitions, or manufacturing scale-up
* 5+ years of team leadership/management role within a PMO, R&D, or Operations function
* Proven experience leading cross-functional initiatives across R&D, Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Supply Chain
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production readiness, and product commercialization
* Familiarity with PLM systems and phase-gate product development processes
* PMP, Six Sigma, or equivalent certification

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field; MBA a plus
* Experience with automation systems, production tooling, and test fixture development
* Deep knowledge of phase-gate execution, PLM milestone management, and portfolio pipeline alignment
* Demonstrated success scaling products from prototype/pilot builds to volume manufacturing
* Experience building and developing technical teams in an R&D or pilot production environment

**What We Offer**

* Generous Paid Time Off – Enjoy 3 weeks of PTO annually, with accrual starting on day one.
* Comprehensive Health Coverage – United Healthcare medical plans available for both individuals and families, starting on the first day of hire in addition to Dental, Vision and Disability Insurance.
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) – Purchase company stock at a 15% discount through convenient payroll deductions.
* 401(k) with Company Match –Receive a 50% match on contributions up to 8%, with immediate vesting so you fully own every dollar right away.
* Paid Holidays – 9 company holidays, plus a floating holiday.
* Tuition Reimbursement –Invest in your future with up to $7,500 per year for approved professional development.

The pay scale is subject to change depending on business needs. Your recruiter can share more about the specific range for your location during the hiring process.*

existing_roles.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

* Own the ISC End-to-End process architecture, defining process standards, documentation requirements, and governance for core ISC value streams.
* Drive process modeling and SIPOC-level design across ISC, working through the Process Modeler and Global Process Owner to ensure clarity of accountability and performance standards.
* Identify and close process design gaps that create risk, inefficiency, or measurement inconsistency across the ISC organization.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Define the Manufacturing Excellence framework for Nouryon, including OEE, TPM, reliability, and asset performance standards applied across the manufacturing network.
* Direct the Manufacturing Excellence Manager to develop and deploy site-level improvement programs, closing the loop between plant performance data and structured intervention.
* Integrate manufacturing excellence priorities into the broader OpEx roadmap, ensuring alignment with Digital Manufacturing, Palantir-enabled analytics, and capital investment decisions.

**People Leadership & COE Development**

* Lead a geographically distributed team of nine direct reports
* Define team structure, role clarity, and succession priorities for the COE
* Build a high-performance COE culture grounded in Nouryon’s Leadership Capability Framework

This role requires approximately 15–25% global travel across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
**Key Performance Indicators**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence COE is measured against the same Breakthrough KPIs as the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing. This alignment is intentional – the COE’s organizational design, capability systems, and governance structures exist to enable these outcomes. Execution is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role is accountable for building and sustaining the organization capable of delivering them.
  

* People Safety
* Process Safety
* FMC — Fixed Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* VMC — Variable Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* OEE — Overall Equipment Effectiveness
* OTIF — On-Time In-Full
* Quality Sigma Level
* CI Activation Rate

**We believe you bring**

* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement, or manufacturing leadership roles in a global, multi-site environment.
* Certified Master Black Belt (MBB) or Black Belt in Lean/Six Sigma, with demonstrated capability to design, govern, and quality-assure a full belt certification program.
* Proven track record of leading change management initiatives in large, matrixed, multi-regional organizations – with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and shift organizational culture.
* Deep knowledge of Manufacturing Excellence frameworks including OEE, TPM, and reliability methodologies, with experience deploying these at scale across a manufacturing network.
* Demonstrated people leadership across multiple geographies and organizational grades, including experience developing high-performing teams in a distributed structure.

**Great if you have**

* Experience in specialty chemicals, process manufacturing, or a similarly regulated, capital-intensive industrial environment.
* Hands-on expertise in End-to-End process design and governance, including SIPOC-level architecture and process ownership models.
* Experience designing and leading corporate Learning & Development programs, including competency frameworks and structured curricula for technical disciplines.
* Prior experience building or structuring a Center of Excellence from the ground up, including team design, governance models, and stakeholder alignment.
* Working proficiency with PowerBI or equivalent reporting platforms for program performance tracking and executive communication.

**We believe you are**
...
  
  
A systems thinker who sees the whole before diving into the parts. You lead through frameworks, not firefighting – you understand that durable operational excellence is built on governance, capability, and culture, not individual heroics. You bring intellectual rigor to every conversation and are comfortable challenging assumptions at any level of the organization, including in rooms where the answer is already assumed.
  
  
You are energized by building – building teams, building programs, building the conditions for others to succeed. You know how to hold standards without being rigid, and how to drive urgency without creating chaos. The right candidate is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in watching a global organization improve because of the systems they put in place – and who brings the patience, persistence, and precision that transformation at scale demands.
  
  
**We offer you**
This is a rare opportunity to architect and lead a newly consolidated global COE with a clear mandate from senior leadership, a defined team, and direct line of sight to enterprise value delivery. You will operate with significant autonomy, build the structure you believe is right, and leave a measurable legacy across a global manufacturing organization at an inflection point in its CI and digital transformation journey.
  
  
At Nouryon, we provide a great job and friendly coworkers, plus benefits in addition to salary.

If you’re looking for your next career move, apply today and join Nouryon’s worldwide team in providing essential solutions that our customers use to manufacture everyday products such as personal care, cleaning, paints and coatings, agriculture and food, pharmaceuticals, and building products. **About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

* Educational: Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Business, or a related field required. Master's degree preferred.

* Deep knowledge of distribution or multi-site operations, including branch execution, warehouse processes, customer service, labor productivity, and operating cost drivers.
* Demonstrated ability to build performance-management systems that connect measures, root causes, ownership, corrective action, and sustained results.
* Practical experience developing standard work, management routines, branch assessments, and scalable operating playbooks.
* Experience leading cross-functional improvement initiatives from business requirements and process design through pilot, rollout, adoption, and sustainment.
* Strong business analytics capability with the ability to validate data, interpret performance, identify meaningful trends, and communicate findings in plain language.
* Working knowledge of warehouse and transportation technology, business intelligence tools, automation, and technology-enabled process improvement.

* Ability to move comfortably between branch-level observation and executive-level decision support.
* Ability to manage competing priorities, establish decision rights, and prevent temporary project support from becoming permanent functional ownership
* Strong follow-through, sound judgment, and a bias toward simple, repeatable solutions that can be sustained by the field.

Our Values
  
  
With every decision and action, we put people first, keep the future in mind, and work as a team toward shared progress.
  
  

* Customer Centric
* Respect
* Collaboration
* Integrity
* Grit

BlueLinx is one of America’s largest distributors of building products, with over 70k branded and private-label SKUs. Headquartered in Marietta, Georgia, we have over 2,000 associates and distribute our comprehensive range of structural and specialty products to approximately 15k national, regional, and local dealers, as well as specialty distributors, national home centers, industrial, and manufactured housing customers.

This role translates strategy into repeatable operating standards, disciplined execution, measurable performance, and scalable support.
  
  
The Director partners with field leadership and cross-functional teams to improve customer experience, delivery performance, carrier accountability, cost effectiveness, and launch readiness, enabling Regional Directors and market leaders to remain focused on field execution.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Planning & Routing**

* Lead the centralized routing organization, establishing operating rhythms, service standards, workload allocation, escalation paths, and accountability.
* Own delivery forecasting, capacity planning, route-planning governance, and resource alignment across AHD markets.
* Develop, document, deploy, and audit routing standards that support safe, efficient, reliable, and customer-focused delivery execution.
* Partner with field leaders to identify capacity constraints, route-quality issues, and execution risks, coordinating corrective actions as needed.

**Operational Excellence**

* Lead the development, maintenance, communication, and adoption of standard operating procedures across Ashley Home Delivery.
* Design and continuously improve end-to-end processes for stand-up, load-out, route monitoring, check-in, returns, recovery, beginning-of-day controls, and end-of-day controls.
* Develop validation, compliance, and audit tools to ensure operating standards are understood, adopted, and sustained.
* Drive continuous improvement through data analysis, root-cause analysis, structured problem-solving, and field feedback.
* Establish governance and documentation processes that preserve institutional knowledge and keep operating standards current.

**3PL & Vendor Management**

* Lead carrier sourcing, due diligence, onboarding, implementation, and performance governance in partnership with Procurement, Legal, Finance, Risk, and AHD leadership.

**Performance Management**

* Establish management routines connecting daily operating controls, weekly business reviews, action plans, and executive-level visibility.
* Analyze performance trends and operational gaps, identify root causes, establish accountable owners, and track corrective actions through resolution.
* Provide decision-ready reporting on customer experience, delivery reliability, productivity, capacity, cost, claims, and carrier performance.

* Coordinate cross-functional implementation activities, manage dependencies and risks, and maintain clear milestones, decisions, ownership, and status reporting.

**People & Organizational Leadership**

**Experience**

Restek is looking for a builder. As our Director of Continuous Improvement, you’ll stand up an enterprise-wide continuous improvement program, developing the systems, the talent, and the Lean culture that make operational excellence part of how we work every day across Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Customer Experience.

Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, you’ll be our principal change agent, leading everything from multi-year transformation programs to focused Kaizen events. Your work will directly shape our strategic priorities by reducing waste and scrap, raising quality, speeding flow, improving the customer experience, and growing profitability.

**What You’ll Do**

Set the Strategy

* Own the multi-year CI roadmap, aligned with Restek’s strategic plan, annual operating plan, and Operations priorities.
* Establish the management system that makes improvement stick (daily management, tiered huddles, A3 problem solving) and define a CI maturity model to guide each function’s progress.
* Partner with Finance to validate savings and ensure improvement gains show up in the P&L.

Lead the Work

* Personally lead and facilitate high-impact Kaizen events, Value Stream Mapping, and transformation projects tied to safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, and customer outcomes.
* Drive measurable gains in OEE, first-pass yield, scrap and rework, on-time delivery, lead time, inventory turns, customer response time, and total cost of quality.
* Make sure improvement work is well scoped, resourced, and sustained, and bring the best practices from inside and outside Restek to every team.

Make an Impact Across the Business

* **Manufacturing:**
  Improve safety, quality, throughput, changeover, and productivity through standard work, visual management, and a Lean production system.
* **Customer Experience:**
  Help deliver an industry-leading experience through faster response and resolution, better processes, and digital enablement.
* **Supply Chain:**
  Strengthen supplier quality and delivery, optimize inventory, and streamline order-to-cash, delivering measurable cost savings.
* **Engineering:**
  Partner on design for manufacturability, new product introduction, and change management to speed time-to-market and build it right the first time.

Build Capability and Culture

* Build, lead, and develop the Continuous Improvement team.
* Design and deliver Restek’s CI training curriculum, including Lean fundamentals, Yellow/Green/Black Belt paths, problem-solving methods, and leader standard work.
* Coach senior leaders and frontline managers in CI thinking, and develop change agents at every level to scale CI beyond the central team.
* Put the metrics and dashboards in place that make progress visible from the manufacturing floor to the executive team, and share wins and learnings across the organization.

**How We Lead at Restek**

Restek leaders model our core values and act as stewards of our culture. They communicate openly, build trust, and support the growth and well-being of their teams. They think globally and act locally, create clarity around goals, hold themselves accountable, partner across functions and regions, and lead with humility and service so every employee-owner can contribute to Restek’s success.

**What You Bring**

**Qualifications:**

The typical requirements for this role include a bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration (master's degree, preferred), or a related field, plus 10 years of progressive operations and CI experience, including at least 5 years in a senior CI or operational excellence leadership role in manufacturing, or the equivalent combination of education and experience.

**Additional Skills & Abilities:**

* A proven track record of leading enterprise-level Lean transformations with sustained, financially validated results.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification (Master Black Belt certification is preferred)
* Hands-on experience across multiple functions (manufacturing, supply chain, quality, customer service, and/or engineering), with credibility on the manufacturing floor and with leadership.
* Experience leading and developing CI practitioners and managers.
* Deep fluency in the CI toolkit: Lean (5S, standard work, visual management, flow, pull, SMED, TPM, Kaizen), Six Sigma (DMAIC, SPC, DOE), Value Stream Mapping, Hoshin Kanri, and structured problem solving (A3, 8D, 5-Why, fishbone).
* Advanced Excel and Power BI (or equivalent) skills for data-driven decision making.
* A servant-leader and coach who thinks strategically, executes in detail, and influences from the manufacturing floor to the Leadership Team, with outstanding written, verbal, and executive presentation skills.

Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment (e.g., FDA, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, GMP) or in scientific instruments, life sciences, chromatography, analytical, or precision-manufactured products and experience bringing digital tools and analytics (e.g., MES, ERP, Power BI, advanced analytics) into the CI toolkit is preferred.

This full onsite position will require the successful completion of a standard background check in accordance with Restek policy. Employment with Restek will require successful completion of a pre-employment drug screen.

**What Makes Restek Unique**

We prioritize work-life balance and well-being with offerings like generous PTO, unlimited sick time, onsite fitness center and wellness program with incentives, childcare reimbursement, and adoption assistance—giving you the tools to Own Your Well-Being. existing_roles.description:
**Location:**
North of Boston, MA (on-site)
  
  
**About The Company**
Our client is a growing, private equity-backed food manufacturer producing fresh, ready-to-cook proteins and meal solutions for leading grocery retailers and foodservice customers nationwide. Their products, including hand-crafted, value-added meats combined with fresh vegetables and seasonings, have earned a strong position in the specialty section of the grocery store. The company is growing, and leadership is now investing in operational excellence to support the next phase of that growth.
  
  
The Opportunity
  
  
This is a newly created role and the company's first dedicated continuous improvement leader. You'll partner closely with plant leadership to build a CI function from the ground up across a 250-person production floor. The operation is high-mix and labor-intensive: much of the product is assembled by hand, the product is perishable, and daily needs change based on customer demand. This is not machine-paced manufacturing, and it calls for someone who knows how to improve operations where people, not equipment, drive output.
  
  
Leadership is excited about this role and fully behind it. The right person will have the independence and support to make a real, measurable impact on cost, yield, and how work gets done.
  
  
What You'll Do
  
  

* Lead cost-out initiatives across the plant, with a focus on labor productivity, yield, and waste reduction
* Build the KPI and metrics foundation the operation currently lacks, including labor standards, yield tracking, and performance dashboards
* Shorten the loop between labor planning and actual results so the team can manage to standard daily
* Rethink how manual work is organized and performed, including line layout, staffing models, work methods, and labor standards for high-mix hand assembly
* Identify and attack sources of product loss, giveaway, and waste in a perishable environment
* Drive structured root cause analysis and make sure fixes stick
* Introduce practical Lean and Six Sigma tools and build a CI culture where none exists today
* Work hands-on on the floor alongside supervisors and team members, coaching and training as you go
* Partner with quality and food safety to make sure improvements support regulatory and customer requirements
* Use NetSuite and Power BI to turn operational data into clear, actionable reporting

What We're Looking For
  
  

* 5+ years of continuous improvement, operational excellence, or industrial engineering experience in manufacturing, with progressive leadership responsibility
* Proven success improving labor-intensive, high-mix, manual assembly operations. This is the most important requirement.
* Food manufacturing experience strongly preferred, especially fresh, perishable, or protein processing environments
* Strong working knowledge of Lean and Six Sigma. Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
* A track record of building metrics, labor standards, and accountability systems from scratch
* Documented cost savings and yield improvements you can speak to in detail
* An independent, self-directed style: someone who can assess an operation, set a plan, and execute without a lot of structure around them
* A hands-on leader who is comfortable on the production floor and earns credibility with frontline teams
* Experience with NetSuite and Power BI, or similar ERP and BI tools
* Bilingual in English and Spanish is a strong plus
* Must be local to the Greater Boston / North Shore area or willing to relocate. This role is on-site.

Why This Role
  
  

* Build the CI function from the ground up with real ownership and visible impact
* Leadership and investors who are committed to the investment and eager to support it
* A growing company with room for advancement as the business scales

**Director of Quality**
=======================

**Colorado Springs, CO | Full-Time | On-Site**

### **Lead Quality. Develop People. Protect the Mission.**

At Cogitic Corporation, quality isn't just a department, it's critical to our mission. We manufacture precision components supporting the U.S. Navy and national defense programs, where accuracy, accountability, and reliability are non-negotiable.

We're seeking an experienced, technically strong Director of Quality to lead our Quality Management System (QMS), develop our inspection team, and drive a culture of operational excellence.

**This is not a desk-only leadership position.** We're looking for someone who can think strategically, lead confidently, and remain technically engaged. The right person is just as comfortable leading an audit or developing a quality strategy as they are reviewing a complex drawing, troubleshooting an inspection challenge, or supporting CMM programming.

If you're a quality leader who takes ownership, develops people, and believes in getting things right the first time, we want to hear from you.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

**Quality Leadership & Team Development**

* Lead, coach, and develop the Quality and Inspection team, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and opportunities for growth.
* Build a high-performing team that values technical excellence, collaboration, continuous learning, and proactive problem-solving.
* Balance strategic quality initiatives with daily operational priorities to support production and delivery commitments.

**Quality Management & Compliance**

* Own, maintain, and continuously improve Cogitic's QMS, ensuring compliance with applicable customer, regulatory, and contractual requirements.
* Lead internal, customer, supplier, and external audits, ensuring findings are addressed effectively and on time.
* Drive corrective action efforts, including root-cause analysis, corrective action implementation, and verification of effectiveness.
* Ensure quality processes support traceability, documentation accuracy, product conformance, and audit readiness.

**Technical Quality & Inspection**

* Oversee inspection planning, testing, and product acceptance for complex, precision-machined components.
* Apply advanced knowledge of engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and dimensional inspection methods.
* Provide hands-on technical support with inspection processes, CMM programming, measurement techniques, and complex quality challenges.
* Maintain oversight of measurement and test equipment (M&TE), calibration programs, and inspection equipment readiness.
* Identify opportunities to improve inspection efficiency, accuracy, and first-pass quality.

**Cross-Functional Partnership & Continuous Improvement**

* Partner closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Mission Assurance, and Supply Chain to resolve quality concerns and execute customer requirements.
* Lead supplier quality activities, including qualification, performance monitoring, audits, and compliance with flow-down requirements.
* Establish and monitor meaningful quality KPIs to identify trends, reduce defects, and drive measurable improvements.
* Leverage ProShop ERP, quality data, and standard quality tools to strengthen processes, reporting, and operational visibility.
* Promote a proactive quality culture focused on prevention, accountability, and doing things right the first time.

**What We're Looking For**
--------------------------

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Quality, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Industrial, Welding Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum of 5 years of manufacturing quality experience, including hands-on machining, inspection, or precision manufacturing exposure.
* Demonstrated experience leading, coaching, and developing technical quality or inspection personnel.
* Strong understanding of AS9100 quality management systems, audit processes, corrective actions, and continuous improvement methodologies.
* Advanced ability to interpret complex engineering drawings, GD&T, specifications, and dimensional tolerances.
* Proven ability to investigate quality issues, identify root causes, implement sustainable solutions, and hold teams accountable.
* Strong technical aptitude, analytical judgment, communication skills, and ability to balance competing priorities.
* Proficiency with ERP systems, Microsoft Office, and technical quality software.
* U.S. citizenship and ability to successfully complete required background screening and meet applicable security clearance eligibility requirements.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting U.S. Navy, NAVSEA, nuclear, or other highly regulated defense manufacturing programs.
* Hands-on experience with CMM programming, inspection planning, and precision measurement equipment.
* Experience managing calibration and M&TE programs.
* Working knowledge of ProShop ERP and SolidWorks or similar CAD software.
* ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), ASME GD&T certification, or comparable credentials.
* Experience with supplier quality management, customer audits, and complex contractual quality requirements.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

In this role, success means more than passing audits. You'll be expected to:

* Build a capable, accountable Quality team that operates with confidence and consistency.
* Maintain an effective, audit-ready QMS that supports the business rather than slowing it down.
* Reduce recurring quality issues through effective root-cause analysis and lasting corrective actions.
* Improve inspection efficiency, product conformance, and on-time execution.
* Develop stronger cross-functional partnerships and establish clear ownership of quality throughout the organization.

**Who Thrives at Cogitic?**
---------------------------

Our strongest leaders demonstrate our core values of **Performance, Character, Courage, Development, and Initiative.**

We're looking for someone who takes ownership instead of assigning blame, addresses challenges directly, coaches rather than simply directs, and understands that quality and operational performance must work together.

You should be comfortable in a growing organization where priorities evolve, expectations are high, and your leadership can make a meaningful impact.

**Compensation & Benefits**
---------------------------

**Compensation:** $150k - 200K annually, based on experience and qualifications.

At Cogitic, we believe in taking care of our team and providing opportunities to grow. Our benefits include:

* **Medical Insurance:** Competitive medical coverage with employer contributions toward premiums.
* **Dental Insurance:** Employer contributes 20% toward dental premiums.
* **Vision Insurance:** Voluntary vision coverage.
* **401(k) Retirement Plan:** Opportunity to save and plan for your future.
* **Life Insurance:** Employer-paid basic life and AD&D coverage.
* **Additional Coverage:** Voluntary life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability options.
* **Paid Time Off:** PTO and 10 company-observed holidays.
* **Professional Development:** Opportunities for continued learning, technical development, and leadership growth.

**Ready to Make an Impact?**
----------------------------

If you're an experienced quality leader who enjoys building strong teams, solving complex manufacturing challenges, and supporting work that matters, we'd love to connect.

**Apply today and help shape the future of Quality at Cogitic Corporation.**

High School Degree and 16+ years’ experience of Compliance and Quality Assurance/Quality Control within Biopharmaceutical or Pharmaceutical manufacturing

Excellent interpersonal, verbal, written and presentation communication skills
