existing_roles.title: Director, Protein Operations
existing_roles.description:
Twist Bioscience is seeking a Director, Protein Operations to lead high-throughput protein production and characterization within our Operations organization. You will run a high-throughput operation that runs seven days a week and lead a large, multi-level team that delivers purified, well-characterized antibodies and proteins to internal programs and external customers on time, at quality, and at cost. The ideal candidate pairs deep expertise in protein expression, purification, and characterization with the rigor to scale a production organization and the drive to automate it.

**Leadership and Operations**

* Lead a large protein production and characterization organization that operates seven days a week, including managers, supervisors, scientists, and associates.
* Own key performance indicators (KPIs) for quality, on-time delivery, turnaround time (TAT), capacity, and cost of goods sold (COGS), and model capacity and staffing against demand.
* Drive continuous process improvement and lead complex investigations, including customer incidents.
* Maintain SOPs, documentation, and training in line with ISO 13485 and other regulatory requirements.

**Protein Production**

* Oversee high-throughput antibody production in HEK293, CHO, and cell-free systems across IgG, Fab, scFv, VHH, and bispecific formats.
* Lead downstream purification of diverse biologics, including bispecific and engineered antibodies.
* Transfer new products and processes from R&D into production and support new product introductions (NPI).

**Protein and Antibody Characterization**

* Oversee Twist's binding, developability, and cell-based functional assay suite, from assay development through execution, analysis, and data reporting, with turnaround times as fast as 1–5 business days.
* Lead binding assessment, including flow cytometry on native antigen, single-point and full kinetics/affinity (KD) by SPR and BLI, and epitope binning by SPR and BLI.
* Lead developability profiling, including analytical size-exclusion chromatography (aSEC), thermostability (nanoDSF), size distribution (DLS), polyspecificity (BVP ELISA, ovalbumin off-target), self-interaction (AC-SINS), and hydrophobic interaction screening.
* Deliver high-quality, consistent datasets that support customer lead selection and AI/ML model training.

**Automation and Scale**

* Partner with Engineering to bring a high level of automation to production and characterization, translating workflows into requirements for liquid handling, robotics, scheduling, and data systems.
* Drive walk-away, high-throughput workflows integrated with LIMS, MES, and SAP to increase capacity, reduce turnaround time, and improve reproducibility.

**Collaboration**

* Partner with R&D, Process Development, Supply Chain, QC, QA, Project Management, and Customer Support to grow the portfolio and meet customer commitments.
* Shape technology and product direction with senior leadership while staying current on antibody discovery, protein expression, and lab automation.

### **What You'll Bring to the Team**

* PhD in protein biochemistry, biological chemistry, immunology, or a related field with 8+ years of experience in biotech, biopharma, or life science tools; or a BS/MS with 12+ years of equivalent experience.
* Experience managing managers and leading large teams, with strong coaching and people development skills.
* A proven track record of scaling protein or antibody production workflows and commercial products.
* Hands-on expertise in mammalian expression, purification (e.g., ÄKTA), and antibody characterization, including SPR/BLI kinetics and epitope binning, flow cytometry, and developability assays (aSEC, nanoDSF, DLS, AC-SINS, polyspecificity).
* Success partnering with engineering teams to implement automated, high-throughput lab workflows.
* Experience owning budgets, KPIs, and capacity planning, with working knowledge of ISO 13485/GMP, Lean, and Six Sigma.
* A strategic thinker who executes tactically, prioritizes well, and influences senior leadership.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience running a high-throughput, made-to-order production operation in the life sciences.
* Experience manufacturing and purifying engineered antibodies.
* Experience with antibody characterization platforms such as Carterra and Octet.
* Familiarity with LIMS, MES, and ERP/SAP systems.

**About Twist Bioscience**

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as "writing" DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care,agriculture, industrial chemicals and data storage, our unique silicon-based DNA Synthesis Platform provides precision at a scale that is otherwise unavailable to our customers.

**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**

**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**Paid time off**

* Four weeks accrued paid vacation
* Two weeks accrued paid sick leave
* Four mental health days
* Two personal days
* Two floating holidays
* Ten holidays

**Benefits**

* All benefits effective on date of hire with no waiting period
* 100% employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employee-only plans
* 100% employer-paid life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability
* 100% employer-paid downtown Atlanta parking or monthly MARTA card
* Affordable plans for legal insurance, critical illness, supplemental life and more
* Immediate eligibility to contribute to a 403(b), plus a 6% employer-paid contribution after one year regardless of employee contributions
* Cell phone stipend
* Employee Donor Advised Fund after one year
* Employee Assistance Program and more

**Culture, Learning & Development**

* Individual Development Plans with training, resources and development opportunities
* Two wellness rooms with self-care resources
* Monthly employee engagement activities

**TO APPLY**

Submit your resume and cover letter through our Careers website.

Note: Only applications submitted through our website will be accepted. Due to the volume of candidates, we are unable to provide status updates or accommodate phone calls or walk-ins regarding open positions.

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

existing_roles.description:
**Job Profile:**

Administrative Operations Manager 3

**Job Family:**

Administrative Operations

**Time Type:**

Full time

**Apply before 11:59 PM Arizona time the day before the posted End Date.**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

Bachelor's degree and seven (7) years of experience appropriate to the area of assignment/field including two (2) years managerial experience; OR, Any equivalent combination of experience and/or training from which comparable knowledge, skills and abilities have been achieved.
  
  
Job Profile Summary:
  
Administers and evaluates business and administrative matters within one department , including budget, operations, and programs and personnel administration.

**Job Description:**

**Salary Range** : $130,000 - $150,000 per year; offer dependent upon experience

  

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE), a leading source of transformative, evidence-based ideas about public education throughout the U.S., is seeking an experienced, strategic, creative, and detail-oriented systems thinker to serve as its Senior Director of Strategic Operations.

As a core member of the leadership team, the Senior Director will shape and lead the systems, processes, and operational strategies that enable CRPE to accelerate its national impact and internal effectiveness. This person will thoughtfully leverage AI, cross-functional collaboration, and relationships across Arizona State University to ensure CRPE operates and deploys talent most effectively as research, technology, and the education contexts change.

The Senior Director will oversee the strategy and execution of CRPE’s core organizational operations, including talent management, grant management, AI integration and adoption, and special projects. Working closely with the Center’s leaders, the Senior Director will ensure that organizational systems, policies, and practices support CRPE’s strategic priorities and reflect its commitment to a strong, inclusive staff culture. This role combines high-level strategic thinking and organizational design with hands-on implementation and problem-solving, designing systems and building the team that runs them.

The Senior Director will supervise a team of three and collaborate closely with other department leaders. CRPE is a remote team and is an especially strong fit for professionals who enjoy building effective systems, navigating complexity, and contributing to a fast-paced, high-impact organization.

**About CRPE**

The Center on Reinventing Public Education (CRPE) is a research organization at Arizona State University’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation, where transformative ideas are rigorously examined and tested, and research informs action. Since 1993, we have remained independent of any single ideology while holding firmly to our core belief that public education is a goal—to prepare every child for citizenship, economic independence, and personal fulfillment—and not a particular set of institutions.

From that foundation, we study what it will take for public education to meet every student’s needs and use those insights to inform meaningful changes in policy and practice.

Our current research explores four broad topics:

* **Students and Families** : We work to understand what students and families need from their education system—and how schools can rise to meet those needs.

* **Systems:** We examine the inner workings of schools, districts, and state governments, delivering insights into how our education systems work to meet the needs of students, families, and communities.

* **Innovations:** We identify promising initiatives outside the traditional education system that have the potential to radically improve teaching and learning, including artificial intelligence, new teacher staffing models, and district-wide innovations.

* **Politics of Change:** We study the critical role of politics in determining whether school systems deliver on their promise, and explore the ways public officials, school system leaders, and change-makers can factor political thinking into their strategies for improving education.

By partnering with the Mary Lou Fulton College, we are uniquely positioned to produce evidence and ideas that lead the country toward an education system that meets the needs of every student. Over the next five years, CRPE will produce ideas and evidence that inform effective state improvement, thoughtful AI policy and implementation, and innovative approaches to ensure every learner is prepared for a boundless future.

  

**Essential Duties:**

*Organizational strategy and change leadership*

* Partner with the CRPE’s Director and Managing Director to lead the organization strategically, helping CRPE adapt its organizational model, structure, and operations as strategy evolves.
* Translate strategy into implementation, turning priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines, and follow-through, and keeping leadership informed through coherent internal communications.
Own organization-wide staffing plans, capacity planning, and project resourcing in partnership with research leaders.  

*AI operational leadership*

* In collaboration with CRPE’s Research Principals, adapt roles, workflows, and tools for the age of AI, bringing in new technology where it improves research and operations.
* Lead AI integration across the organization, including policy and guidance, staff training and office hours, playbooks, piloting and scaling new uses, and building staff buy-in and tracking adoption.
Ensure staff have the systems, software, and equipment they need, and that data integrity, security, and records retention protocols are in place to adhere with University guidelines.  

*Talent strategy and people operations*

* Develop and implement a strategy to attract, retain, develop, and promote talent and support an inclusive workforce, drawing on a flexible mix of full-time staff, part-time staff, interns, and contractors.
* Lead CRPE’s annual performance review cycles, aligned with university requirements.
* Lead culture initiatives, including all-staff meetings, the annual staff retreat, professional development, and supporting staff and supervisors through feedback, to build a positive, respectful culture.
Supervise, coach, and develop a team of three: the People and Operations Manager, the Project Coordinator, and the Grants Manager.  

*University partnership manager*

* Serve as CRPE’s lead liaison and negotiator with ASU department leads, including HR, finance, sponsored projects, and IT partners. Find solutions within university systems and advocate effectively for CRPE’s needs.
Build collaborative relationships with other ASU colleges and units that advance CRPE’s mission.  

*Financial strategy and oversight*

Supervise and partner with the Grants Manager to oversee CRPE’s long-range financial strategy, including annual spending plans, multi-year forecasts, and funding and runway planning.  



*Oversight of special projects*

Lead or sponsor cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives that vary in complexity, urgency, and frequency as needs arise.  

  

**Desired Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in business, public administration, or a related field preferred.
* AI fluency and change leadership. Hands-on proficiency with generative AI tools and demonstrated experience leading organizational adoption of new technology, including developing policy, training staff, and building buy-in across teams with varied comfort levels.
* Talent and performance management. Experience designing and running recruitment, including coaching supervisors and managing contractor relationships.
* Complex project management. Experience leading multiple concurrent, cross-functional projects to completion amid shifting priorities and tight timelines. A track record of diagnosing operational challenges and building better systems.
Operations management. Experience overseeing financial and operational systems, including budget management and forecasting, grants administration, and human resources, in a nonprofit, education, or university setting (preferred).  

  

**Working Environment:**

* Activities are performed in an environmentally controlled office setting and involve extended periods of sitting, keyboarding, and use of a computer mouse.
* Position may require travel between campus locations or buildings for meetings or job-related tasks.
* Regular activities require the ability to manage and adjust to changing priorities, including handling time-sensitive tasks and resolving conflicts.
* MLFC supports flexible work options for certain positions, such as alternate work schedules and hybrid or full remote arrangements, subject to approvals per ASU policy.

**Department Statement:**

ASU’s Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation creates knowledge, mobilizes people, and takes action to improve education. Nationally recognized as a leader in teacher preparation, leadership development and scholarly research, Mary Lou Fulton College for Teaching and Learning Innovation prepares over 8,000 educators annually. MLFC faculty create knowledge by drawing from a wide range of academic disciplines to gain insight into important questions about the process of learning, the practice of teaching and the effects of education policy. MLFC mobilizes people through bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs, through non-degree professional development programs and through socially embedded, multilateral community engagement. MLFC takes action by bringing people and ideas together to increase the capabilities of individual educators and the performance of education systems.

  

Aligned with ASU’s charter , MLFC is committed to advancing inclusive excellence in our curricula, programming and institutional relationships.

Arizona State University is a new model for American higher education, an unprecedented combination of academic excellence, entrepreneurial energy and broad access. This New American University is a single, unified institution comprising four differentiated campuses positively impacting the economic, social, cultural and environmental health of the communities it serves. Its research is inspired by real world application blurring the boundaries that traditionally separate academic disciplines. ASU serves more than 100,000 students in metropolitan Phoenix, Arizona, the nation's fifth largest city. Elevate is committed to providing the highest quality commercial roofing, wall and lining systems to solve our customers’ challenges, grounded by a 45-year legacy of proven experience. Our mission is to deliver solutions that save time, perform reliably and protect our communities. We are devoted to building partnerships rooted in trust in reflection of our Elevate promise that Nobody Covers You Better™.
  
  
Elevate is part of the Amrize family of brands. Visit ElevateCommercialBP.com to learn more.
  
  
We’re seeking a Director of Quality Assurance who’s ready to be part of a people-first company offering best-in-class products, exceptional training, and deep industry pride—all built to help our partners and team succeed.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Quality Assurance Director strategically leads the development, implementation, and maintenance of comprehensive quality evaluation and control systems across the organization. This includes overseeing the design and analysis of inspection and testing processes, ensuring the precision and accuracy of products and equipment, driving root cause analysis for incidents, and establishing compliance with reliability standards and documentation requirements to uphold the highest levels of product quality and operational excellence
  
  
**What You'll Accomplish**

* Strategic Oversight - Overseeing and directing the overall operations of quality assurance within a company to ensure continuous improvement and compliance. This involves defining and promoting a quality mindset across the entire company.
* Quality Management System - Developing and implementing quality management systems to ensure product and service quality, and maintaining and improving quality standards, policies, and procedures.
* Compliance & Regulatory Oversight - Ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulations, and company policies, and coordinating with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* Quality Control, Claim Mgmt, Supplier Quality - Overseeing quality control processes to ensure products meet quality standards, and conducting regular quality audits and inspections to identify and address quality issues.This also includes establishing and enforcing quality standards, testing materials and products, and developing raw material and in-process product inspection standards.
* Continuous Improvement - Leading continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency, and implementing best practices to reduce defects and improve processes. This can involve applying tools such as CAPA, SPC charts, Root Cause Analysis, and FMEA, and leading Six Sigma or Lean initiatives.
* Leadership & Team Development - Leading and mentoring the quality assurance team, fostering a culture of high performance and professional development, and ensuring the team has the necessary skills and resources. Responsible for generating a culture of collaboration across the organization.
* Budget & Financial Management - Achieving financial objectives by preparing the quality assurance budget, scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions.
* Customer Experience - Gathering customer feedback through gemba and data collection on quality andperformance, ensuring products meet or exceed customer expectations, and implementing changes based on feedback
* Demonstrate a commitment to communicating, improving and adhering to health, safety and environmental policies in all work environments and areas.
* Promote a culture of safety and exhibit these behaviors.

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Mgmt, or related discipline from an accredited university or college.
* At least 8 y+ years of relevant quality, continuous improvement, manufacturing experience including at least 5 years management or direct/indirect leadership experience.
* 3+ years of QMS / ISO9001 or similar experience required.
* CMQ/QE, CQE, CQA are all preferred.
* Six Sigma certification preferred.

**Additional Requirements**

* Successful candidates must adhere to all safety protocols and proper use of Amrize approved Personal Protection Equipment ("PPE"), including but not limited to respirators.
* Employees that are required to wear respirators must be clean shaven where the respirator seal meets the face in order to pass the qualitative and quantitative fit tests.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary
* Retirement Savings: Choose from 401(k) pre-tax and/or Roth after-tax savings
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Medical, Dental, Disability and Life Insurance
* Holistic Health & Well-being programs
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) & Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) for health and dependent care
* Vision and other Voluntary benefits and discounts
* Paid time off & paid holidays
* Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity)
* Educational Assistance Program

**Director of Quality**
, you will lead the quality strategy and continuous improvement efforts across all Bison manufacturing sites. You will be responsible for ensuring that the products meet or exceed customer expectations, industry standards, and regulatory requirements while driving overall quality performance and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to establish and maintain effective quality systems, drive process improvements, and ensure compliance with industry certifications.
  
  
This position can be based at either our
**Whitsett, NC**
or
**Reynosa, MX**
facility.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  

* Leadership & Strategy

+ Develop and execute a strategic quality plan in alignment with business unit goals.
+ Lead, mentor, and develop a team of quality professionals across two locations, ensuring consistency in processes and objectives.
+ Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

* Quality Management Systems (QMS)

+ Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and improvement of the QAD Elements QMS and other relevant Quality Management Systems at both locations. Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry-specific quality standards (e.g., FDA, ISO, AS9100, etc.).
+ Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of quality management systems and propose enhancements to improve overall performance.

* Process & Product Quality

+ Collaborate with sales, operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to identify drive resolution of quality issues, ensuring process and product integrity.
+ Support root cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for internal and external quality issues.
+ Oversee first article inspections, process capability studies, and validation/qualification activities to ensure robust manufacturing processes.

* Continuous Improvement

+ Lead Lean Six Sigma or other continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing defects, enhancing efficiency, and improving overall quality.
+ Implement data-driven decision-making tools (e.g., SPC, FMEA, Control Plans) to monitor and improve process capabilities.
+ Facilitate cross-functional value stream mapping sessions and quality workshops to drive process improvements.

* Customer & Supplier Relations

+ Serve as the main point of contact for customer quality issues, audits, and feedback, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
+ Oversee supplier quality management, including audits, performance monitoring, and supplier development initiatives.

* Metrics & Reporting

+ Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to quality performance, including scrap/rework, defect rates, customer complaints, and audit findings.
+ Regularly report quality performance metrics to senior leadership, highlighting trends and recommending corrective actions.

* Regulatory Compliance & Audits

+ Lead internal and external audits, ensuring the sites comply with relevant standards and certifications.
+ Ensure the manufacturing facilities are audit-ready at all times and coordinate responses to audit findings.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in quality management within a manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience with quality management systems (ISO 9001, AS9100, FDA, or equivalent) and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma).
* Demonstrated ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and to reduce costs. The successful candidate must be able to identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.
* Proven track record of driving quality improvements across multi-site operations.
* Ability to travel as needed to the BU manufacturing sites (up to 30%)
* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency in quality tools such as SPC, FMEA, 8D, and Root Cause Analysis.

Incentive: Yes

**Job Title**
- Executive Director, Quality Assurance
  
  
**Department**
- Quality Assurance
  
  
**Work Location**
- Cranbury NJ (On-site)
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Head of U.S. Quality provides strategic, scientific, and operational leadership for Quality Assurance and Quality Control across U.S. operations. The role is accountable for maintaining an effective, risk-based Quality Management System and ensuring that research, development, clinical, CMC, and manufacturing activities comply with applicable global regulations, industry standards, company policies, and client expectations. The position drives quality excellence, inspection readiness, organizational capability, and continuous improvement, with particular emphasis on biologics, commercial manufacturing, and complex CDMO operations.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
Strategic Quality Leadership
  
  

* Provide strategic and scientific leadership for the U.S. quality organization and execute the global Quality strategy in alignment with company standards, policies, and business objectives.
* Lead Quality Assurance and Quality Control functions supporting R&D, Clinical, CMC, technology transfer, manufacturing, and commercial operations.
* Embed quality considerations into strategic planning, new services, product development, site improvement, and organizational growth decisions.
* Serve as the senior Quality representative with clients, partners, regulatory authorities, external auditors, and industry forums.

Quality Management System and Compliance
  
  

* Establish, govern, monitor, and continuously improve a robust, risk-based Quality Management System and related procedural framework.
* Provide oversight of change control, deviations, investigations, CAPA, quality risk management, document control, training, validation, data trending, and management review.
* Ensure controlled documentation, including SOPs, master and executed batch records, validation protocols and reports, and technical reports, is accurate, current, and compliant.
* Identify and implement systemic improvements based on compliance trends, quality metrics, inspection outcomes, industry benchmarks, and emerging regulatory expectations.

Regulatory and Inspection Readiness
  
  

* Ensure ongoing compliance with applicable GxP and cGMP requirements, including FDA, EMA, NMPA/CFDA, ICH, USP, EP, and Chinese Pharmacopoeia expectations where applicable.
* Lead regulatory inspections and client audits, including inspection preparation, health-authority interactions, response strategy, remediation, and effectiveness monitoring.
* Maintain current knowledge of global regulatory requirements, industry trends, and best practices, and translate changes into timely updates to systems, procedures, and training.

Quality Assurance and Product Disposition
  
  

* Provide leadership and direction for QA oversight of manufacturing and laboratory operations, including batch record review, product disposition, quality events, and release decisions.
* Oversee review and approval of critical quality and technical documentation and ensure quality decisions are scientifically sound, risk-based, timely, and well documented.
* Facilitate quality risk assessments and mitigation plans to anticipate and address potential product, process, compliance, and supply risks.

Quality Control and Laboratory Governance
  
  

* Ensure Quality Control laboratories are appropriately equipped, staffed, and governed to support in-process, release, stability, and other required testing.
* Oversee analytical method development, qualification/validation, transfer, lifecycle management, laboratory investigations, and data integrity controls.
* Use laboratory and environmental monitoring trends, KPIs, and leading indicators to inform risk management, resource allocation, and improvement priorities.

Supplier, Material, and Client Quality
  
  

* Oversee supplier qualification, material quality, quality agreements, and the quality governance of raw materials and components used in manufacturing.
* Lead quality-related client communications, support client governance, participate in audits, and ensure observations and commitments are addressed effectively.
* Build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders while protecting compliance, product quality, patient safety, and client satisfaction.

Operational Excellence and Cross-functional Partnership
  
  

* Drive continuous improvement and operational excellence across Quality operations using data, trends, metrics, and appropriate problem-solving methodologies.
* Partner with Manufacturing, R&D, CMC, Clinical, Engineering, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and other functions to resolve complex quality issues and sustain compliant operations.
* Provide cross-functional support to ensure the sustainability and continual improvement of quality and compliance systems across the organization.

People, Organization, and Financial Leadership
  
  

* Build, recruit, lead, and develop a high-performing, diverse Quality organization with clear accountabilities, succession plans, and capability-development priorities.
* Manage the employee lifecycle for direct reports, including selection, hiring, onboarding, goal setting, coaching, development, performance discussions, and recognition.
* Establish meaningful quality performance metrics and regularly evaluate organizational effectiveness, capacity, and capability against business needs.
* Prepare and manage the Quality budget and expenditures, and support capital expenditure requests for quality, laboratory, site improvement, and renovation needs.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree or higher in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biological Engineering, or a related scientific or engineering field; an advanced degree is preferred.
* At least 15 years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including at least 10 years in Quality leadership or Quality management roles.
* Extensive experience in a GMP-regulated biopharmaceutical, biologics, or CDMO environment; experience with antibody-drug conjugates is highly desirable.
* Demonstrated commercial manufacturing experience and broad knowledge of R&D QA, GLP, Clinical, CMC, Manufacturing QA, and QC environments.
* Proven experience leading cross-functional Quality organizations in complex, multi-site, or international settings.
* Deep knowledge of global GxP regulations, Quality Management Systems, regulatory inspections, and compliance frameworks.
* Experience interacting directly with regulatory authorities, clients, auditors, and strategic partners.
* Proven ability to lead large-scale programs, organizational change, quality improvement initiatives, and inspection remediation.

Leadership Competencies and Skills
  
  

* Strategic and systems thinking with the ability to connect quality risk, regulatory expectations, operational performance, and business priorities.
* Strong people leadership, organization-building, coaching, succession planning, and change-management capability.
* Excellent communication, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills at executive, client, and regulatory levels.
* Strong analytical, statistical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills for complex and ambiguous quality issues.
* Demonstrated commitment to quality culture, data integrity, scientific rigor, patient safety, and continuous improvement.
* Ability to operate effectively across cultures, functions, sites, and global time zones.

Physical and Travel Requirements
  
  
The role may require occasional domestic and international travel to support client meetings, regulatory inspections, conferences, partner interactions, and oversight of external or multi-site quality activities.
  
  
Role Success Measures
  
  

* An effective, sustainable, and inspection-ready Quality Management System.
* Consistent regulatory compliance and timely closure of audit, inspection, and quality commitments.
* Robust product disposition, laboratory, supplier, and quality-event governance.
* Data-driven continuous improvement and measurable reduction of recurring quality risks.
* A capable, engaged, and accountable Quality organization aligned with U.S. and global business needs.
* Strong, transparent, and trusted relationships with clients, regulators, partners, and internal stakeholders.

**The salary range for this position is $193,000 - $329,000**
**An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability**

**SUPERVISION EXCERCISED**

**Essential Duties And Responsibilities**

* Build a high-performance quality culture and team, empowering and holding direct reports and cross-functional teams accountable for successful quality and compliance transformation. Leads with authority and influences globally across manufacturing and distribution facilities and cross functional stakeholders including but not limited to quality, product development, process technology, operations, supply chain, procurement, regulatory affairs, finance, and human resources.

Provide strategic direction and communication of the quality transformation goals, creating a clear vision and integration with overall business objectives. * Support interactions with regulatory bodies and ensure compliance with all applicable quality and safety standards. Responsible for leading the team with the review and finalizing any responses to regulatory authorities in collaboration with the Chief Quality Officer.
* Lead the identification, analysis, and resolution of quality issues and non-conformities across various departments in collaboration with the Quality Systems and CAPA teams. Ensure remediation efforts are managed through the QMS.
* Foster a culture of quality and continuous improvement within the organization. Promote the use of lean and Six Sigma methodologies to enhance quality and operational efficiency. Stay abreast of industry trends and advancements in quality management and remediation practices.
* Guide the activities required of the quality organization to ensure compliance with all appropriate regulations and standards, including FDA Part 820, ISO 13485, CMDR, MDR, MDSAP, and JPAL. Ensures compliance and readiness globally in collaboration with the QMS.

**Qualifications And Experience Requirements**
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for this position:
  
  

* Bachelor's degree is required, in engineering, science or closely related technical discipline is preferred. A master’s degree preferred.
* 18+ years of experience leading a team (direct reports or projects) or equivalent education and years of management experience
* Experience in highly regulated industries required, medical device and/or pharmaceutical preferred, including material remediation experience

* Knowledge of process design and implementation, change control, auditing, and document management systems required, general knowledge of statistical analysis preferred.
* Demonstrated organizational, management and communication skills. Proven track record of cross-functional collaboration across teams and change management skills. Strong ability to influence across all levels of the organization, including senior leadership. Experienced with interacting with Executive leadership to execute decisions and manage risk.

**Description**

**Company & Job Overview:**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Manufacturing is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in Operations leadership, particularly in a medical device, medical technology or biotechnology organization. They will possess deep expertise in talent management, organizational development, and workforce planning.

This position is an office-based position at the company’s Irvine, CA headquarters.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Execution**

* Translate corporate vision into actionable operational strategies, setting short- and long-term objectives for scaling manufacturing and supply chain.
* Oversee Profit & Loss (P&L) for the operations division, managing budgets, and identifying areas for continuous cost optimization.
* Serve as a core member of the executive leadership team, collaborating cross-functionally with R&D, Quality, Regulatory, and Commercial teams.

**Manufacturing & Supply Chain Management**

* Direct all manufacturing operations (internal facilities and/or outsourced/CMO partnerships), ensuring production schedules are met with the highest standards of safety and quality.
* Oversee global supply chain, procurement, and logistics, mitigating risks related to material shortages and distribution delays.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce lead times, and improve manufacturing efficiency.

**Quality Assurance & Regulatory Compliance**

* Partner closely with Quality/Regulatory to uphold and enforce compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, and other global regulatory requirements.
* Maintain a culture of compliance and continuous improvement, proactively addressing audits, CAPAs (Corrective and Preventive Actions), and non-conformances.
* Guarantee that all products are manufactured, tested, and released according to defined specifications.

**New Product Introduction (NPI) & Scaling**

* Partner closely with R&D during the design transfer phase to ensure new products are manufacturable, cost-effective, and ready for commercial scale.
* Manage capacity planning, facility expansions, and capital expenditure (CapEx) projects to support product pipeline growth.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing operations team, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and operational excellence.

**Requirements**

**Required Skills & Abilities**

* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust across all levels of the organization.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on data-driven decision-making.
* Ability to navigate complexity and lead in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
* Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach to operational excellence.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering (Biomedical, Mechanical, or Industrial), Business Administration, or a related technical field. Master’s degree or MBA strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 15-20 years of progressive operations leadership experience in the medical device, life sciences, or heavily regulated manufacturing industry.
* Lifecycle Track Record: At least 5 years of experience in a startup or rapid-growth environment actively guiding a complex medical device through the transition from R&D to commercial launch.
* Product Complexity: Proven technical expertise managing Class II or Class III active (electromechanical) medical devices involving fluidics, software, or sterile disposables.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated expertise in talent management, organizational development, and Operations strategy.
* Proven success in managing change and leading cross-functional teams in a global setting.

**Preferred Attributes**

* Deep expertise in Quality Management Systems (QMS), FDA regulations (cGMP), and ISO 13485.
* Strong track record of managing global or complex supply chains and contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs).
* Exceptional P&L management skills with proven ability to drive CapEx planning and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Proven capability to lead transformational change, manage risk, and foster cross-functional teamwork.

**Travel**

* Ability to occasionally travel domestically

**Physical Requirements**

* The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

**Working Environment**

This position primarily works in an office environment. It requires frequent sitting, standing and walking. Daily use of a computer and other computing and digital devices is required. May stand for extended periods when facilitating meetings or walking in the facilities.

The information contained in this job description is for compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and is not an exhaustive list of duties performed for this position.

protected_roles.description:
**About This Role**
The Head of Corporate Quality is responsible for creating and managing the Global Biogen Quality Management System (QMS). The main areas of focus include Quality Systems, internal and external audits for cGMP compliance (including external vendors and CMOs), IT Quality, Technical Product Complaints, and Central Knowledge Management (including documentation).
  
  
This role is central to Quality and PO&T, managing risk, compliance performance, staying compliant with regulatory changes, and seeking opportunities to gain efficiency and effectiveness in the administration of PO&T’s cGMP systems. Additionally, the role is accountable for preparing semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS and informing Executive Management of potential business risks due to a changing regulatory environment or systemic issues within the company. This role also serves as the principal liaison with the R&D Clinical Compliance organization and provides guidance for ICH conformance. Oversight includes biologic products, ASOs, small molecule products, gene therapy, devices, digital, and combination products.
  
  
*This role is hybrid- RTP or hybrid- Cambridge based.*
**Travel requirements**
: 25% – 50% depending on location. More travel required if not located in RTP.
  
  
**What You’ll Do**

* Implement integrated quality systems, policies, and standards applicable to all Biogen U.S. and international manufacturing sites and PO&T locations, including Baar, Cambridge, Netherlands, Solothurn, and RTP.
* Develop and maintain a risk assessment process for evaluating and monitoring all cGXP systems.
* Ensure regulatory inspection responses are assessed holistically.
* Establish clear goals and effective metrics that provide insight into industry benchmarks and applicable trends regarding cGMP compliance.
* Oversee external monitoring of regulatory updates (domestic and international) and incorporate changes into Biogen’s QMS as needed.
* Internal and external GxP and ISO audit programs, including risk management and audit program oversight.
* Ensure Biogen’s internal manufacturing sites, Quality Systems, and vendors operate in a state of cGMP compliance, with any risks appropriately communicated and escalated.

**IT QA Department**

* Oversee GxP IT computerized systems across Biogen, including underlying infrastructure.
* Define appropriate standards and manage lifecycle documentation and supporting processes to ensure compliant implementation and management through retirement.

**Lifecycle Management**

* Oversee process and compliance-related content (specifically documentation, including governing policies, process documents, and other similar GxP documents) in the electronic document management system.
* Protect, index, classify, and archive GXP records, digitally preserve vital records, manage records lifecycle, and translate GMP content needed in multiple languages.
* Oversee the PO&T training program, providing global guidance and standards to ensure appropriate GxP training is conducted.

**Technical Product Complaint Department**

* Develop and maintain policies and procedures to manage complaints in line with industry and regulatory standards.
* Identify strategy and provide direction to team members regarding complaint investigation, root cause analysis, CAPAs, regulatory responses, and launch readiness for new products.
* Ensure trending and reporting of complaint cases and metrics, including appropriate escalation and response to significant events.

**Global Management Review (GMR)**

* Act as the chair for the GMR, ensuring ongoing management review and awareness of Biogen Quality and compliance performance (in accordance with cGMP and ICH expectations).
* Prepare semi-annual executive-level updates on the state of Biogen’s QMS based on GMR outcomes.
* Establish short and long-term goals, objectives, and strategies for the Global Corporate Quality organization.
* Ensure appropriate policies and procedures are in place to measure, monitor, and report "actual" versus "planned" results.
* Drive major projects and programs for the Organizational Unit or Function to completion within schedule and budget.
* Manage multiple cost centers and determine the development of overall objectives and long-range goals of the organization.
* Interact directly with senior representatives of regulatory agencies, including the FDA and EMEA.
* Manage direct reports and managers of managers to increase their performance and effectiveness.

**Who You Are**
You are a seasoned leader in the pharmaceutical industry with an expert understanding of both U.S. and international regulatory requirements. Your influence within an organization is felt through consistent execution and strong leadership competencies. With excellent communication and change management skills, you're adept at leading and implementing change. You thrive in a highly regulated environment and have comprehensive knowledge of the pharmaceutical product development process.
  
  
**Qualifications**
**Required Skills:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a related field with a minimum of 15 years of leadership experience in the pharmaceutical industry.
* Minimum of 10 years’ experience leading a Quality Assurance, Regulatory, or Corporate organization at the Director+ level in a highly regulated environment, preferably in biotech, pharmaceutical, or similar industry.
* Experience with the FDA, EMEA, and preferably multiple additional regulatory agencies in other foreign countries.
* Experience in clinical and commercial products as well as both large and small molecule programs, device, and combination products is strongly preferred. ASQ or other auditing certification is beneficial.
* Quality and Compliance experience consistent with worldwide regulatory requirements.
* Expert knowledge of US and International cGxPs, ISO, ICH, and Device regulations.
* Ability to hire and retain top talent with a track record of developing leaders.
* Excellent knowledge of the pharmaceutical product development process, ICH, and device regulations.
* Ability to influence the organization through consistent execution of Biogen leadership competencies.
* Strong leadership abilities required to effectively manage highly capable and high-performing teams.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and implement change, including excellent communication and change management skills.

**Preferred Skills**

* Advanced degree (PharmD, PhD)

Job Level: Management
  
  
**Additional Information**
The base compensation range for this role is: $281,000.00-$397,250.00
  
  
Base salary offered is determined through an analytical approach utilizing a combination of factors including, but not limited to, relevant skills & experience, job location, and internal equity.
  
  
Regular employees are eligible to receive both short term and long-term incentives, including cash bonus and equity incentive opportunities, designed to reward recent achievements and recognize your future potential based on individual, business unit and company performance.
  
  
**Benefits**
In addition to compensation, Biogen offers a full and highly competitive range of benefits designed to support our employees’ and their families
*physical, financial, emotional,*
and
*social well-being*
; including, but not limited to:
  
  

* Medical, Dental, Vision, & Life insurances
* Fitness & Wellness programs including a fitness reimbursement
* Short- and Long-Term Disability insurance
* A minimum of 15 days of paid vacation and an additional end-of-year shutdown time off (Dec 26-Dec 31)
* Up to 12 company paid holidays + 3 paid days off for Personal Significance
* 80 hours of sick time per calendar year
* Paid Maternity and Parental Leave benefit
* 401(k) program participation with company matched contributions
* Employee stock purchase plan
* Tuition reimbursement of up to $10,000 per calendar year
* Employee Resource Groups participation

**Why Biogen?**
We are a global team with a commitment to excellence, and a pioneering spirit. As a mid-sized biotechnology company, we provide the stability and resources of a well-established business while fostering an environment where individual contributions make a significant impact. Our team encompasses some of the most talented and passionate achievers who have unparalleled opportunities for learning, growth, and expanding their skills. Above all, we work together to deliver life-changing medicines, with every role playing a vital part in our mission. Caring Deeply. Achieving Excellence. Changing Lives.
  
  
At Biogen, we are committed to building on our culture of inclusion and belonging that reflects the communities where we operate and the patients we serve. We know that diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives make us a stronger and more innovative company, and we are focused on building teams where every employee feels empowered and inspired. Read on to learn more about Biogen.
  
  
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, race, color, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, religion, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other basis protected by federal, state or local law. Biogen is an E-Verify Employer in the United States.

**Vice President, Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
  Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
  Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
  Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
  Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
  Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
  Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
  Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
  Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
  Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
  Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.
